title: The Ten-Percent Ceiling: Ibn Khaldun's Fiscal Curve and Pakistan's Tax Record, 2001–2025
abstract: Question. Pakistan has raised its statutory tax rates repeatedly for a quarter of a century — general sales tax from 16% to 18%, a new super tax up to 10%, a 29% corporate rate stacked with surcharges — yet its tax-to-GDP ratio has not durably risen. Is the country on the wrong side of the fiscal curve Ibn Khaldun described in 1377, where higher rates shrink the base faster than they raise the yield? Claim. Yes — on the evidence available, Pakistan sits past the peak of its Khaldunian curve. Over 2001–2024 the tax-to-GDP ratio moved only inside a 7.9–11.4% band (mean 9.7%), and the Federal Board of Revenue's own ratio stayed in single digits for 24 consecutive fiscal years (2000-01 to 2023-24), while statutory rates rose at every margin. The binding constraint is the base, not the rate: about 5.9 million returns were filed for tax year 2025 in a country of 241.5 million people, and only about 3 million taxpayers show any taxable income at all. Falsifier. The claim is refuted if either (i) the FBR-only tax-to-GDP ratio rises above 12% and holds there for three consecutive fiscal years with no new statutory rate increase, or (ii) a legislated cut in a major rate — general sales tax back to 16%, or super-tax relief — is followed within two fiscal years by a fall, rather than a rise, in the FBR tax-to-GDP ratio. The fiscal year 2025-26 outturn (target Rs 14.131 trillion) is the first scheduled test. Identification. Association only. This is a descriptive time-series test on published aggregates, with no control group and no randomised or quasi-experimental variation in rates. Confounders — GDP growth, inflation, IMF programme conditions, enforcement drives — are named, not controlled. The paper falsifies the claim that "rate rises raise the ratio"; it does not estimate a causal effect of any single rate. A regression-discontinuity design on the February 2023 GST rise (17% → 18%) and a randomised rate pilot are proposed as the causal tests. One clean number: 24 years below 10% — the number of consecutive fiscal years the FBR's tax-to-GDP ratio stayed in single digits while rates rose. The stakes number is 3 million: the people in a country of 241.5 million who show any taxable income. Keywords: Ibn Khaldun; Laffer curve; tax-to-GDP ratio; Pakistan; FBR; fiscal policy; tax base; super tax; maqasid; 'adl.
summary: Question. Pakistan has raised its statutory tax rates repeatedly for a quarter of a century — general sales tax from 16% to 18%, a new super tax up to 10%, a 29% corporate rate stacked with surcharges — yet its tax-to-GDP ratio has not durably risen.

title: The 260-Metre Ceiling: A Falsifiable Attribution of Lahore's November Smog Peak to Domestic Sources and Seasonal Meteorology, with a Smog-Budget Policy for Punjab
abstract: Question. Is Lahore's November smog peak driven mainly by polluted air crossing the border from India, or by domestic emissions amplified by the seasonal collapse of the atmosphere's mixing height? Claim. The November peak is driven predominantly by domestic emissions — transport, domestic crop-residue burning, waste burning, industry and brick kilns — amplified by the collapse of the mixing height from 830–860 m in May–June to about 260 m in November, a ~3.2-fold compression of the air available to dilute the same emissions. Transboundary inflow is a secondary contributor, estimated at 13–30% across published studies. Falsifier. The claim would be refuted if a November smog episode showed (i) PM2.5 rising faster in border cities than in inland cities, while (ii) HYSPLIT back-trajectories showed air masses reaching Lahore from the east, and (iii) TROPOMI NO2 columns at the border exceeded Lahore's. The 8–10 November 2026 Diwali episode tested all three conditions and produced the opposite pattern: inland cities (Faisalabad, Multan) rose by 85 µg/m³ against 36 µg/m³ in border cities, Delhi air stayed at least 266 km from Lahore, and Lahore — not the border — is Punjab's strongest TROPOMI NO2 hotspot (92.31 µmol/m²). Identification. Natural experiment (the Diwali window as an exogenous transboundary shock) with a spatial gradient (distance from the border as the dose). Not an RCT; no single-source causal effect size is estimated. The paper falsifies the transboundary-dominant hypothesis; it does not prove exact domestic shares. One clean number: 260 metres — Lahore's November mixing height, the ceiling under which a city of ~14 million people breathes. The stakes number is 3.9 years: the average life expectancy air pollution removes from a Pakistani, up to 7 years in Lahore. Keywords: Lahore smog; PM2.5; mixing height; Sentinel-5P TROPOMI; source apportionment; transboundary air pollution; Punjab; khilafah; smog budget.
summary: Question. Is Lahore's November smog peak driven mainly by polluted air crossing the border from India, or by domestic emissions amplified by the seasonal collapse of the atmosphere's mixing height? Claim.

title: Four Captopril Stereoisomers Dock Within 0.07 kcal/mol on VIM-2 While Their Measured Potencies Span 76-Fold: Rigid Docking Is Blind to the Stereochemistry That Defines MBL Inhibition
abstract: VIM-2 is a B1 metallo-beta-lactamase that hydrolyses almost all beta-lactams including carbapenems, and no clinically useful inhibitor exists for it. The best measured inhibitor in the reference set, taniborbactam (Ki 0.02 µM), cannot be docked by AutoDock Vina at all because it contains boron, which Vina's PDBQT parser rejects — a tool limit the standard pipeline run for this paper hit and could not pass. The testable question that remains is whether rigid docking can resolve the potency gap between stereoisomers of the same molecule: D-captopril inhibits VIM-2 at 0.072 µM, L-captopril at 4.4 µM, and the two epi-isomers at 5.5 µM each, a 76-fold range from a single stereocentre flip, with crystal structures showing different binding modes. We docked all four stereoisomers with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on 4C1E, the 1.40 angstrom VIM-2 structure co-crystallised with D-captopril. The scores are minus 6.16, minus 6.19, minus 6.12 and minus 6.19 kcal/mol — a total span of 0.07 kcal/mol, thirty times smaller than Vina noise, with rank correlation against measured potency of 0.15. The screen cannot see the stereochemistry that defines this inhibition. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay IC50 comparison of the four stereoisomers on VIM-2 with a metal-aware rescoring of the same poses: if the measured 76-fold gap reproduces while every rescoring still ties them, the failure is confirmed as a scoring-function limit, not a pose-sampling error.
summary: VIM-2 is a B1 metallo-beta-lactamase that hydrolyses almost all beta-lactams including carbapenems, and no clinically useful inhibitor exists for it.

title: Nintedanib Tops a PknB Docking Rank That Matches Measured Potency Exactly: Two Approved Cancer Kinase Inhibitors and the Mitoxantrone Caveat
abstract: PknB is an essential serine/threonine kinase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and no PknB inhibitor has reached the clinic: the best published inhibitors are nanomolar in vitro and only micromolar against whole cells. We docked five compounds with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on 3ORK, the 1.60 angstrom structure of the PknB kinase domain (L33D mutant) with an ATP-gamma-S analogue in the ATP site: nintedanib, two matched-pair aminopyrimidine/pyrazole inhibitors from the same series, sunitinib, and mitoxantrone, the literature PknB inhibitor. The docking rank matches the measured potency rank exactly (Spearman rho 1.0, n = 4): nintedanib, Kd 3.6 nM, docks at minus 9.70 kcal/mol; the matched pair, Ki 13 and 17 nM, at minus 8.66 and minus 8.30; sunitinib, Kd 87 nM, at minus 8.24. Mitoxantrone, which has no attached PknB potency number and is excluded from the correlation, docks worst at minus 7.19 and carries a PAINS alert with the maximum Tox21 read-across for the DNA-damage assays SR-ATAD5 and SR-p53. Two approved cancer kinase inhibitors top a tuberculosis kinase ranking, and the literature inhibitor is the weakest and the most toxic — a clean repurposing signal and a warning in the same table. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay PknB kinase comparison of the four ranked compounds with a whole-cell assay on Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv: if nintedanib again measures most potent on the enzyme but fails on whole cells, the gap is confirmed as permeability, not potency.
summary: PknB is an essential serine/threonine kinase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and no PknB inhibitor has reached the clinic: the best published inhibitors are nanomolar in vitro and only micromolar against whole cells.

title: Cilomilast Out-Scores Roflumilast on PDE4D Despite a 171-Fold Potency Gap, and Crisaborole Cannot Be Docked at All: Rigid Docking Misses the Contact Points That Define PDE4 Inhibition
abstract: Phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) is the target of four approved drugs — roflumilast, apremilast, crisaborole and difamilast — and a 2025 structural study proposed a simple rule for their potency: roflumilast preserves all three active-site contact points (metal-ion site, conserved glutamine, water network), apremilast two, crisaborole one, and the measured IC50s follow the rule (0.7 nM, 0.14 µM, 0.24 µM). We docked the three dockable drugs with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on 3G4L, the 2.5 angstrom human PDE4D structure co-crystallised with roflumilast. Cilomilast, the weakest of the three docked by 171-fold, scores best at minus 9.62 kcal/mol; roflumilast scores minus 9.14 and apremilast minus 8.93. The 171-fold potency gap between roflumilast and cilomilast is 0.48 kcal/mol in the wrong direction, and the rank correlation against measured potency is 0.5 (n = 3). Crisaborole, the third drug in the comparison set, cannot be docked at all: it is a benzoxaborole, and Vina rejects boron — the second boronate this run has failed to dock, after taniborbactam on VIM-2. The screen cannot see the contact points that define PDE4 potency, and it cannot see the boronate that defines the class's newest chemistry. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay PDE4D IC50 comparison of the four drugs with a metal-aware rescoring of the same poses: if the measured 200-fold range reproduces while every rescoring still ties them, the failure is confirmed as a scoring-function limit, not a pose-sampling error.

title: MRTX1133 Re-Docks at −12.71 kcal/mol on the KRAS G12D Switch-II Pocket and Sotorasib Scores Worst: A Corrected Docking Benchmark After a Wrong-Target Pipeline Run
abstract: KRAS G12D is the commonest KRAS allele, driving about 42% of KRAS-mutant pancreatic cancers, and it has no approved inhibitor: the covalent KRAS G12C drugs cannot work because G12D has no cysteine to bind. MRTX1133 is the first non-covalent, selective KRAS G12D inhibitor, with a pERK IC50 of 2 nM in AGS cells, but the standard pipeline run for this paper resolved the target to the wrong enzyme and docked it into the wrong pocket, so both numbers from that run are discarded here and the correction is documented in full. We docked MRTX1133, three analogues from the same discovery paper, and the G12C inhibitor sotorasib as a negative control with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on 7RPZ, the 1.3 angstrom KRAS G12D structure co-crystallised with MRTX1133 in the switch-II pocket. MRTX1133 re-docked at minus 12.71 kcal/mol; the analogues scored minus 11.62, minus 11.13 and minus 9.34 against measured pERK IC50s of 24, 530 and 24 nM; sotorasib scored worst at minus 7.74, as a G12C drug should on G12D. Rank correlation against measured potency is moderate (Spearman rho 0.65, n = 4), but two compounds with identical measured potency differ by 2.28 kcal/mol in docking, and the re-dock sits 2.52 kcal/mol clear of its own second pose. The screen ranks the series roughly right and cannot resolve equal potencies. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay pERK comparison of the four Wang-series compounds in one KRAS G12D cell line: if compounds 25 and 36 again measure identically while docking differs by more than 2 kcal/mol, the gap is confirmed as a scoring artefact, not a potency signal.
summary: KRAS G12D is the commonest KRAS allele, driving about 42% of KRAS-mutant pancreatic cancers, and it has no approved inhibitor: the covalent KRAS G12C drugs cannot work because G12D has no cysteine to bind.

title: Ibrutinib Re-Docks at −10.86 kcal/mol on Its Own BTK Structure, but Four Sub-Nanomolar Covalent Inhibitors Score Worse: Rigid Docking Cannot Price the Cys481 Bond
abstract: Ibrutinib, the first covalent Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor, binds irreversibly to Cys481 in the ATP pocket, and the C481S mutation — cysteine replaced by serine — removes that bond and is the commonest cause of acquired resistance in chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL). The question this paper tests is whether a standard rigid-docking screen can rank covalent BTK inhibitors at all, given that the scoring function cannot price a covalent bond. We docked ibrutinib and four ChEMBL BTK ligands with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on 5P9J, the 1.08 angstrom BTK kinase domain co-crystallised with ibrutinib itself. Ibrutinib re-docked at minus 10.86 kcal/mol. All four test compounds carry the same acrylamide warhead and are measured at 0.04 to 0.05 nM against BTK in ChEMBL — roughly ten times more potent than ibrutinib's 0.5 nM — yet they docked worse: minus 10.13, minus 9.47, minus 8.64 and minus 8.43 kcal/mol. Rank correlation between docking score and measured potency is inverted (Spearman rho minus 0.63, n = 5): the most potent compound measured docks worst. The screen validates the protocol (the reference drug re-docks well on its own structure) and fails as a ranking tool for covalent inhibitors in the same run. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay kinase comparison of the four compounds against wild-type and C481S BTK: if their C481S IC50s collapse like ibrutinib's while pirtobrutinib's holds, the warhead series is covalent-only and the docking inversion is confirmed as a scoring artefact, not a potency signal.
summary: Ibrutinib, the first covalent Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor, binds irreversibly to Cys481 in the ATP pocket, and the C481S mutation — cysteine replaced by serine — removes that bond and is the commonest cause of acquired resistance in chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL).

title: Multi-target computational triage of known bioactive chemical space against seven disease targets: similarity screening, ADMET/toxicity read-across and AutoDock Vina docking (week of 9-15 Nov 2026)
abstract: We screened the bioactive chemical space of ChEMBL against seven therapeutically relevant targets in one week of automated LeadForge runs (9–15 Nov 2026): Plasmodium falciparum dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (PfDHODH), Staphylococcus aureus enoyl-ACP reductase (FabI), tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2), cyclin-dependent kinase 7 (CDK7), myeloid cell leukemia 1 (MCL1), peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARG) and respiratory syncytial virus fusion protein F (RSV F). For each target, the reference drug was recovered from live ChEMBL data (rediscovery check), 44–58 known ligands were similarity-screened (FabI: 430 compounds via a pinned-target run; TYK2: PubChem fallback after a ChEMBL outage), leads were ranked on a composite of similarity, Lipinski/Veber drug-likeness, PAINS and kNN toxicity read-across, and the top five leads were docked with AutoDock Vina against the best available X-ray structure, with the reference drug re-docked as control. Four runs produced leads that docked better than their reference drug: PfDHODH (all five leads, best −9.72 vs −8.21 kcal/mol for DSM265), FabI (three leads, best −11.44 vs −10.15 for afabicin), CDK7 (two leads, best −9.98 vs −8.91 for samuraciclib) and MCL1 (two stereoisomer leads, best −9.33 vs −8.26 for S63845), plus PPARG (one lead, −10.26 vs −9.05 for pioglitazone). Two runs were honest negatives (TYK2: closest lead 0.19 kcal/mol behind deucravacitinib, inside noise; RSV F: no novel lead beat presatovir). The RSV F run also caught and corrected a structure-selection error: the auto-picked PDB 29QJ is an HR1 fragment with a stapled peptide, not the presatovir pocket, and the comparison was re-run at prefusion structure 6VKE. All findings are computational triage; no compound is claimed as a drug, and wet-lab validation is required.

title: Pinning the Cosmic Shoreline with JWST: LTT 1445 A b and c Are Airless Above the Line, LHS 1140 b Keeps Its Helium Below It
abstract: Two results published in November 2026 test the cosmic shoreline — the I ∝ v_esc^4 boundary that separates rocky planets with atmospheres from airless worlds — from opposite sides. The JWST Rocky Worlds programme reports MIRI/F1500W secondary eclipses of LTT 1445 A b and c (Ih et al., arXiv:2611.17300): eclipse depths of 157(+18/−17) and 154(+54/−37) ppm give 15-µm brightness temperatures of 528(+39/−29) K and 625(+109/−79) K, both consistent with dark bare rock; for b, CO2 partial pressure is <0.6 mbar and surface pressure ≲0.1 bar. LTT 1445 A b is the closest planet to the shoreline yet observed in eclipse. In the same week, ground-based spectroscopy reported metastable helium escaping from the habitable-zone super-Earth LHS 1140 b in 2024 but not in 2025 (Cherubim et al., Science 2026), while four JWST NIRISS transits rule out helium at the reported level (Radica 2026; Bennett et al. 2026). We place all three planets on the classical Mars-anchored XUV shoreline, I_XUV = (a⊕/a)^2 (L*/L⊙)^0.4, and find LTT 1445 A b 2.3× above the line, LTT 1445 A c 11.9× above it, and LHS 1140 b 8.5× below it — every planet on its predicted side. The two results bracket the shoreline zero point to log10 I_XUV = 4 log10 v_esc + D with D in [−4.10, −2.81], against the canonical −3.17. We state this as a falsifiable claim: any substantial atmosphere found on a rocky planet more than 0.36 dex above the classical line, or any bare rock more than 0.93 dex below it, falsifies the classical zero point; simultaneous ground- and space-based helium transits of LHS 1140 b will decide whether its lower bound stands. Keywords: exoplanet atmospheres; cosmic shoreline; atmospheric escape; JWST; M dwarfs; LTT 1445; LHS 1140 b; helium
summary: Two results published in November 2026 test the cosmic shoreline — the I ∝ v_esc^4 boundary that separates rocky planets with atmospheres from airless worlds — from opposite sides.

title: Sorbitol Dehydrogenase Inhibitors Show No Rank Correlation on Three Docking Centres — and SORD Inhibition Already Failed to Help Diabetic Nerves in Rats
abstract: Sorbitol dehydrogenase (SORD) catalyses the second step of the polyol pathway, oxidising sorbitol to fructose. Its inhibitors were developed as a treatment for diabetic neuropathy, on the logic that blocking fructose formation should help. We benchmarked rigid AutoDock Vina docking against measured human SORD inhibition data for five Pfizer piperazino-pyrimidine sorbitol dehydrogenase inhibitors (SDIs), including the reference compound CP-166572. Three human SORD structures exist in the Protein Data Bank. The pipeline picked 1PL8 — the highest-resolution structure — but 1PL8 is an NAD+ complex with no inhibitor, and its automatic centre fell on the NAD+ cofactor centroid, 11.62 Å from the catalytic Zn2+. We ran two corrected dockings: one centred on the catalytic Zn2+ of 1PL8, and one on 1PL6, the inhibitor-bound structure, whose co-crystallised ligand is CP-166572 itself. On the NAD+ centre the most potent measured inhibitor — CHEMBL90344, IC50 27 nM — scored worst (−6.61 kcal/mol), and the rank correlation against measured potency was Spearman ρ = −0.2 (n = 4). On the Zn2+ centre all five compounds fell inside a single 0.79 kcal/mol band and ρ = +0.2. On the correct, inhibitor-bound structure the correlation was ρ = +0.35, and the re-dock control failed outright: CP-166572, re-docked into its own crystal structure, scored weakest of the five (−6.20 kcal/mol). No centre ranks the compounds. The result is consistent with the published animal record: in streptozotocin-diabetic rats the SORD inhibitor WAY-135706 lowered fructose but corrected neither nerve conduction velocity nor endoneurial blood flow, while an aldose reductase inhibitor corrected both; and biallelic loss-of-function SORD mutations cause hereditary motor neuropathy in humans, meaning pharmacological SORD inhibition mimics a disease-causing state. SORD is a weak target for diabetic neuropathy, and rigid docking without a metal-aware model cannot rank its inhibitors. Keywords: sorbitol dehydrogenase; SORD; polyol pathway; diabetic neuropathy; molecular docking; AutoDock Vina; CP-166572; Pakistan
summary: Sorbitol dehydrogenase (SORD) catalyses the second step of the polyol pathway, oxidising sorbitol to fructose. Its inhibitors were developed as a treatment for diabetic neuropathy, on the logic that blocking fructose formation should help.

title: Rigid Docking Gets the Extremes Right on SARS-CoV-2 Mpro: the 0.04 nM Analogue Scores Best and Nirmatrelvir Ties for Last
abstract: Nirmatrelvir, the active component of Paxlovid, is a covalent inhibitor of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro, nsp5). We benchmarked rigid AutoDock Vina docking against measured inhibition data for nirmatrelvir and four analogues (Ki 0.04–3.1 nM), docked into the nirmatrelvir-bound structure 7SI9 (2.0 Å). This is the first positive rank correlation in this series: Spearman ρ = +0.48 (n = 5). The most potent analogue (Ki 0.04 nM) scored best (−8.79 kcal/mol), nirmatrelvir itself (Ki 3.1 nM, consensus of ten ChEMBL records) tied for last (−8.22 kcal/mol), and the re-dock control worked — nirmatrelvir re-docked into its own crystal structure with tight poses (−8.22, −8.21, −7.93 kcal/mol). But the method compresses the differences: the measured potencies span 77-fold (~2.6 kcal/mol) while the docking scores span only 0.57 kcal/mol, so the middle of the ranking is noise. Two pipeline lessons are recorded: the first automated run used the wrong ChEMBL target (maltase-glucoamylase) and the wrong structure (the NSP3 macrodomain), with every dock failing; and the pipeline's top activity record for nirmatrelvir (Ki 0.26 nM) is an outlier against ten records at 3.0–3.11 nM. Rigid docking can rank Mpro analogues at the extremes, but not in the middle — and it cannot score the covalent bond that does much of the work. Keywords: SARS-CoV-2; main protease; Mpro; nirmatrelvir; Paxlovid; molecular docking; AutoDock Vina; covalent inhibitor
summary: Nirmatrelvir, the active component of Paxlovid, is a covalent inhibitor of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro, nsp5). We benchmarked rigid AutoDock Vina docking against measured inhibition data for nirmatrelvir and four analogues (Ki 0.04–3.1 nM), docked into the nirmatrelvir-bound structure 7SI9 (2.0 Å).

title: ATP-Competitive mTOR Inhibitors Are All Sub-Nanomolar but Docking Spreads Them Over 1.78 kcal/mol — and Ranks Them Backwards
abstract: The mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) is a serine/threonine kinase that controls cell growth and is frequently deregulated in cancer. First-generation mTOR drugs (rapalogs such as everolimus) are allosteric: they bind the FRB domain via FKBP12 and block substrate recruitment. Second-generation inhibitors compete directly with ATP in the kinase domain and inhibit both mTOR complexes. We benchmarked rigid AutoDock Vina docking against measured mTOR inhibition data for five ATP-competitive inhibitors (IC50 0.10–0.20 nM), docked into the Torin2-bound kinase-domain structure 4JSX (3.5 Å). The five compounds are essentially equipotent in the assay — a two-fold range, equivalent to ~0.4 kcal/mol — but docking spread them over 1.78 kcal/mol (−7.67 to −9.45 kcal/mol) and ranked them backwards (Spearman ρ = −0.4, n = 5): the 0.20 nM compound scored best (−9.45 kcal/mol) and the 0.13 nM compound scored worst (−7.67 kcal/mol). The negative control could not be scored at all: everolimus, a 958-Da macrolide with ~30 rotatable bonds, crashed the docking run (Vina non-zero exit after ~20 min of compute), so no ATP-site score was obtained. The method invents differences where the assay sees near-equality, and it cannot even run the reference drug. Two pipeline lessons are recorded: the automated PDB lookup hung on the structure search, and its <3.0 Å resolution filter can never select a kinase-domain structure for mTOR, because every structure better than 3.0 Å is an FRB-domain fragment. Docking scores should not prioritise analogues among sub-nanomolar mTOR inhibitors. Keywords: mTOR; kinase inhibitor; everolimus; Torin2; molecular docking; AutoDock Vina; ATP-competitive; cancer
summary: The mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) is a serine/threonine kinase that controls cell growth and is frequently deregulated in cancer. First-generation mTOR drugs (rapalogs such as everolimus) are allosteric: they bind the FRB domain via FKBP12 and block substrate recruitment.

title: Rigid Docking Separates Genuine Trypanothione Reductase Inhibitors from Miltefosine but Ranks the Series Backwards
abstract: Trypanothione reductase (TR) is the flavoenzyme that keeps the trypanothione redox system of Leishmania and Trypanosoma parasites reduced; humans have no equivalent enzyme, which makes it a selective antiparasitic target. Leishmania donovani TR has no deposited crystal structure, so we docked against the Leishmania infantum homologue (87.2% sequence identity), structure 4ADW, centred on the bound physiological substrate trypanothione. We benchmarked rigid AutoDock Vina docking against measured inhibition data for four β-carboline–quinazolinone TR inhibitors (Ki 0.8–9.2 µM), with miltefosine — the oral clinical drug for visceral leishmaniasis, which is not a TR inhibitor — as a negative control. Docking separated the classes cleanly: the four genuine inhibitors scored −7.75 to −8.56 kcal/mol, while miltefosine scored −4.54 kcal/mol, a gap of at least 3.21 kcal/mol. Within the inhibitor series, however, the ranking was inverted (Spearman ρ = −0.6, n = 4): the two weakest measured inhibitors (Ki 7.2 and 9.2 µM) scored best (−8.56 and −8.40 kcal/mol), and the most potent (Ki 800 nM) ranked third (−8.13 kcal/mol). All four inhibitors fell inside a 0.81 kcal/mol band — one noise band — while their measured potencies span 11.5-fold. Rigid docking can tell a TR inhibitor from a non-inhibitor, but it cannot rank this series. The result supports TR as a target — the first-line antimonials act through it — while warning that docking scores alone should not prioritise analogues for synthesis. Keywords: trypanothione reductase; Leishmania donovani; Leishmania infantum; visceral leishmaniasis; molecular docking; AutoDock Vina; miltefosine; β-carboline
summary: Trypanothione reductase (TR) is the flavoenzyme that keeps the trypanothione redox system of Leishmania and Trypanosoma parasites reduced; humans have no equivalent enzyme, which makes it a selective antiparasitic target.

title: Ponatinib Scores −14.36 kcal/mol on BCR-ABL1 T315I and Imatinib Scores the Same on Wild Type and Mutant: Rigid Docking Fails the Gatekeeper Negative Control
abstract: Imatinib transformed chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML), but the T315I gatekeeper mutation — threonine 315 replaced by isoleucine — removes the hydrogen bond imatinib needs and sterically blocks the ATP pocket, conferring resistance to imatinib, dasatinib and nilotinib. Ponatinib was designed around this mutation, and asciminib now offers a myristoyl-pocket alternative, but no docking screen has been tested against the gatekeeper as a negative control. We docked ponatinib, imatinib and three ChEMBL ABL1 ligands (a GNF-7-series type-II inhibitor and two DFG-out hybrid ureas) with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on three murine Abl1 kinase-domain structures: wild type 3KFA (1.22 angstrom) and 3OXZ (2.2 angstrom, ponatinib-bound), and the T315I mutant 3OY3 (1.95 angstrom, AP24589-bound). Ponatinib re-docked at minus 14.33 kcal/mol on its own wild-type structure and scored minus 14.36 on T315I — indistinguishable, matching its measured sub-nanomolar potency on both forms (0.37 nM wild type, 2.0 nM T315I). But imatinib scored minus 10.41 on wild type and minus 9.60 on T315I, a 0.81 gap inside Vina noise, although its measured potency collapses from 10.8 nM on wild type to essentially inactive on T315I. The three other ligands cluster at minus 9.29 to minus 9.92 on both structures, and the choice of wild-type structure alone moves ponatinib's score by 2.79 kcal/mol — more than the mutation does. Rank correlation against measured ABL1 IC50s is weak (Spearman rho 0.5 on wild type, 0.6 on T315I, n = 5). The screen validates ponatinib's pan-BCR-ABL profile and fails its negative control in the same run. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay kinase comparison of ponatinib, imatinib and the GNF-7-series compound on wild-type and T315I ABL1: if imatinib's T315I IC50 is more than 100-fold weaker while its docking score is unchanged, rigid docking is confirmed blind to gatekeeper resistance.
summary: Imatinib transformed chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML), but the T315I gatekeeper mutation — threonine 315 replaced by isoleucine — removes the hydrogen bond imatinib needs and sterically blocks the ATP pocket, conferring resistance to imatinib, dasatinib and nilotinib.

title: Vina Ranks the Weakest Measured PBP2a Binder First: Zero Rank Correlation on Two MRSA Acyl-Enzyme Structures
abstract: MRSA caused more than 100,000 deaths attributable to antimicrobial resistance in 2019, and its resistance rests on a single protein, PBP2a, encoded by mecA, whose closed active site excludes most beta-lactams; ceftaroline overcomes this by binding an allosteric site 60 angstrom away, opening the active site for a second molecule to acylate Ser403, and clinical N146K/E150K mutations disrupt that trigger. The gap this paper attacks is whether a standardised docking screen can rank PBP2a binders at all. We docked four ChEMBL MecA actives with measured Kd/IC50 values, ceftaroline (prodrug and active form), ceftobiprole and the carbapenem analogue L-695,256 into two acyl-enzyme structures — 1MWS (2.00 A) and the ceftaroline co-crystal 3ZG0 chain B (2.60 A) — with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 under one protocol, centres audited to 0.0 A from the co-crystallised ligands. The rank test failed on both structures: the Vina order (CHEMBL4862632 first) is unrelated to the measured order (CHEMBL4847813, Kd 129 nM, first), Spearman rho = 0.0, and the second-best measured binder, CHEMBL4879273 (Kd 168 nM), docked worst on both structures. A second independent Vina run reproduced the same order, and one ChEMBL ligand turned out to be ceftobiprole itself, the same molecule scoring 1 kcal/mol apart under two SMILES representations. No "beats ceftaroline" claim can be made from this screen, and Vina's non-covalent scores cannot model the covalent acylation that is ceftaroline's mechanism. The falsifiable next step is a PBP2a acylation assay (k2/Ks) of the four ChEMBL ligands against ceftaroline in wild-type and N146K/E150K PBP2a: if the measured acylation order matches the ChEMBL record rather than the Vina order, docking alone must not be used to prioritise PBP2a leads on these structures.

title: Momelotinib Re-Docks Best on JAK2 (8BXH) With a PAINS Alert, and the Rank Correlation Flips Sign Between Kd and IC50
abstract: JAK2 inhibitors transformed myelofibrosis care: ruxolitinib first in 2011, then fedratinib, pacritinib and momelotinib, all ATP-competitive inhibitors of the same JH1 kinase domain, differing mainly in their selectivity and in which cytopenias they worsen or spare. The question is whether a standard docking screen can rank them by their measured potency on the JAK2 structure. We docked six compounds into 8BXH, the JAK2 JH1 structure co-crystallised with momelotinib (1.3 angstrom), with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 under one protocol: the four myelofibrosis drugs, plus tofacitinib and baricitinib as cross-class comparators. Momelotinib re-docked best at minus 9.73 kcal/mol, ruxolitinib scored minus 8.73 and pacritinib worst at minus 7.67. The rank test depends on which potency measure is used: against the four drugs' IC50 values the Spearman rho is 0.2, against their Kd values it is minus 0.4, both on four compounds, so the screen has no defensible rank signal either way. Momelotinib also carries the screen's only PAINS alert, despite being an approved drug, and the most selective drug in the set, pacritinib at 26-fold over JAK1, docks worst — a property the single-target screen cannot measure at all. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay kinase comparison of all six compounds on JAK2, with JAK1 selectivity measured on the same plates: if the measured order matches the Kd record rather than the Vina order, docking alone must not be used to prioritise JAK2 inhibitors on this structure.
summary: JAK2 inhibitors transformed myelofibrosis care: ruxolitinib first in 2011, then fedratinib, pacritinib and momelotinib, all ATP-competitive inhibitors of the same JH1 kinase domain, differing mainly in their selectivity and in which cytopenias they worsen or spare.

title: Urease Inhibitors Dock Weakly Without Ni2+ on H. pylori Urease (1E9Z), and Clarithromycin Is Rejected at +45.73 kcal/mol
abstract: Helicobacter pylori infects about half the world's population — a pooled prevalence of 48.5 percent, roughly 4.4 billion people in 2015 — and it survives stomach acid because its urease converts urea to ammonia, neutralising the acid around it. Acetohydroxamic acid is the only FDA-approved urease inhibitor, and it is a weak one. The question is whether a standard docking screen can rank urease inhibitors on the H. pylori enzyme. We docked eight compounds into 1E9Z, the H. pylori urease structure (3.00 angstrom), with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 under one protocol: acetohydroxamic acid, flurofamide, thiourea, hydroxyurea, clarithromycin as a regimen negative control, and three PubChem analogues of acetohydroxamic acid. The scores are all weak, from minus 3.47 to minus 5.35, because the two nickel ions that drive real urease inhibition are absent from the docking — Vina cannot model nickel coordination and the receptor preparation drops the ions. Among the measured inhibitors the direction matches the literature: flurofamide, about a thousand times more potent than acetohydroxamic acid in intact cells, docks best at minus 5.19, and acetohydroxamic acid at minus 4.84 beats hydroxyurea at minus 4.67, matching their jack-bean IC50s of 42 and 100 micromolar. The screen's one clean result is the rejection: clarithromycin, which kills H. pylori by binding the ribosome and not by inhibiting urease, scores plus 45.73, a repulsive pose the pocket cannot accommodate. The falsifiable next step is a urease inhibition assay of flurofamide, acetohydroxamic acid, hydroxyurea and the best analogue, PubChem 75743, on purified H. pylori urease: if flurofamide is the most potent and clarithromycin shows no inhibition, the directional signal holds; if any analogue beats flurofamide, it becomes the lead for a urease-inhibitor series.
summary: Helicobacter pylori infects about half the world's population — a pooled prevalence of 48.5 percent, roughly 4.4 billion people in 2015 — and it survives stomach acid because its urease converts urea to ammonia, neutralising the acid around it.

title: Rivaroxaban Docks Worst on Its Own Factor Xa Structure (2W26): a Negative Rank Correlation for Three Direct Oral Anticoagulants
abstract: Factor Xa sits at the convergence of the intrinsic and extrinsic coagulation pathways, and the direct oral anticoagulants that inhibit it — rivaroxaban, apixaban and edoxaban — replaced warfarin for most indications because they need no routine monitoring and have fixed dosing. The question is whether a standard docking screen can rank them by their measured potency on the factor Xa structure. We docked eight compounds into 2W26, the factor Xa structure co-crystallised with rivaroxaban itself (2.08 angstrom), with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 under one protocol: the three anticoagulants, betrixaban and four PubChem analogues of rivaroxaban. The reference drug rivaroxaban docked worst of all eight at minus 7.97 kcal/mol, 1.51 below the best compound, an unmeasured analogue at minus 9.48. Among the three drugs with measured Ki values, the rank test fails in the wrong direction: apixaban, the most potent at 0.08 nM, docks second at minus 8.75, edoxaban, the weakest at 0.56 nM, docks first at minus 8.79, and rivaroxaban, at 0.4 nM, docks last, giving Spearman rho of minus 0.5 on three compounds. The two best-scoring compounds in the screen are analogues with no measured potency at all, so the screen produces no lead claim. The falsifiable next step is a chromogenic factor Xa assay of the three drugs and the two best analogues on the same plates: if the measured IC50 order matches the Ki record rather than the Vina order, docking alone must not be used to prioritise factor Xa inhibitors on this structure.
summary: Factor Xa sits at the convergence of the intrinsic and extrinsic coagulation pathways, and the direct oral anticoagulants that inhibit it — rivaroxaban, apixaban and edoxaban — replaced warfarin for most indications because they need no routine monitoring and have fixed dosing.

title: CH7233163 Re-Docks Best and Osimertinib Near Worst on Triple-Mutant EGFR (6LUB): a Directional Signal, Not a Ranking
abstract: Third-generation osimertinib is the standard first-line therapy for EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer, but the C797S mutation removes the cysteine its covalent warhead needs, and no fourth-generation inhibitor is yet approved. The question is whether a standard docking screen can separate a genuine fourth-generation binder from the failed drug on the triple-mutant kinase. We docked ten compounds into the triple-mutant structure 6LUB (EGFR L858R/T790M/C797S, 2.315 angstrom) with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 under one protocol: the fourth-generation tool compound CH7233163, osimertinib, gefitinib, afatinib, brigatinib and five PubChem analogues of osimertinib. The co-crystallised ligand CH7233163 re-docked best at minus 9.53 kcal/mol, 1.38 clear of the next compound, while osimertinib scored minus 7.50 and gefitinib minus 7.27, the weakest in the set. The direction matches the measured record: CH7233163 inhibits the triple mutant at 0.28 nM biochemically and 20 nM in cells, whereas osimertinib needs 1.42 micromolar to stop triple-mutant BaF3 cells. But only two compounds in the set carry measured triple-mutant potencies on any assay, and those two were measured in different assay types, so no rank correlation can be computed and the five analogues, scoring minus 7.27 to minus 8.01, carry no measured potency at all. The screen is therefore a directional signal, not a ranking, and the re-dock of a co-crystallised ligand is expected to score well because the pocket is shaped around it. The falsifiable next step is a kinase assay of CH7233163, brigatinib and the best analogue, PubChem 121280087, against osimertinib on L858R/T790M/C797S EGFR in one assay: if CH7233163 is the most potent and osimertinib the least, the directional signal holds; if any analogue beats brigatinib, it becomes the lead for a fourth-generation series.
summary: Third-generation osimertinib is the standard first-line therapy for EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer, but the C797S mutation removes the cysteine its covalent warhead needs, and no fourth-generation inhibitor is yet approved.

title: One variant, two proteinopathies: APOE Christchurch (R136S) as a heparan-sulfate-gated brake on tau and α-synuclein seeding — a structural hypothesis and a testable therapeutic programme
abstract: Background. APOE is the strongest genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease, and a rare variant — APOE3 Christchurch (APOE3ch, R136S) — protected a PSEN1 E280A carrier from dementia for roughly 28 years despite extensive amyloid deposition. Until November 2026 the protection was understood as a tau story: R136S weakens apolipoprotein E (ApoE) binding to heparan sulfate proteoglycans (HSPGs), limiting tau spread. New evidence. Soto-Faguás and colleagues (Cell Reports, 11 November 2026) now report that the Christchurch mutation engineered into mouse ApoE also prevents the accumulation of α-synuclein — the protein of Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia — in predisposed mice, with the senior author describing it as acting "like a super-APOE-2". Hypothesis. We propose a single shared mechanism: tau and α-synuclein seeds both enter neurons through the same HSPG gateway, and R136S closes that gateway for both. We test the structural premise on the real human sequence (UniProt P02649): residues 136–150 form a cationic cluster (Arg136, Arg142, Lys143, Arg145, Lys146, Arg147, Arg150) carrying a net charge of +7; R136S removes one positive charge (+7 → +6) and shifts the N-terminal domain net charge to −4 — the same value as protective APOE2, versus −2 for risk-conferring APOE4. Falsifiable claim. If the shared-gateway model is correct, recombinant ApoE3ch will reduce α-synuclein preformed-fibril uptake into primary neurons by a comparable fraction to its reduction of tau uptake, and any Christchurch-mimetic that occupies the ApoE HSPG-binding pocket will inhibit α-synuclein seeding as well as tau seeding. We specify the experiments, effect-size expectations, and the observations that would falsify the model. Conclusion. One rare variant may define one druggable gateway for two diseases — and, because women with Parkinson's disease dementia carry a substantially higher amyloid co-pathology burden, the benefit of closing that gateway should be tested with sex-stratified analysis.
summary: Background. APOE is the strongest genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease, and a rare variant — APOE3 Christchurch (APOE3ch, R136S) — protected a PSEN1 E280A carrier from dementia for roughly 28 years despite extensive amyloid deposition.

title: Four Whole-Cell-Active Compounds Dock Into S. Typhi GyrB at −8.39 to −9.41 kcal/mol, But Azithromycin Cannot Be Docked and the Potencies Are Phenotypic, Not Gyrase Binding
abstract: Extensively drug-resistant (XDR) typhoid — resistant to ampicillin, chloramphenicol, co-trimoxazole, fluoroquinolones and ceftriaxone — emerged in Hyderabad, Sindh in late 2016 and now accounts for roughly 70% of Salmonella Typhi in Pakistan, leaving azithromycin as the last oral option, with resistance already appearing. The gap this paper attacks is whether a standardised docking screen can find a DNA gyrase binder better than azithromycin for XDR typhoid. We ran the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P0A2I4 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL614448, 5 bioactivities → PubChem → RDKit ADMET/PAINS → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7) and docked four whole-cell-active compounds into the 2.2 Å S. Typhi GyrB structure 6J90, with the grid centre audited to the co-crystallised ATP centroid. All four leads docked strongly — CHEMBL3585716 −9.41, CHEMBL5171589 −9.28, CHEMBL3585709 −9.27, CHEMBL3585717 −8.39 kcal/mol — but azithromycin itself could not be docked at all (the Vina run timed out at the pipeline's 900-second limit on the 749 Da macrolide), so no "beats azithromycin" claim can be made, and the docking order does not track whole-cell potency (Spearman ρ = −0.20, n = 4, p = 0.80). Critically, no S. Typhi DNA gyrase target exists in ChEMBL at all — the potencies used here are phenotypic whole-cell data, not gyrase binding data — so this screen tests a hypothesis (does whole-cell potency track GyrB binding?) rather than validating one. The falsifiable next step is a GyrB ATPase inhibition assay of the four leads against azithromycin with whole-cell MICs: if a lead inhibits GyrB at concentrations matching its MIC, it is a genuine GyrB-targeting candidate; if it does not, its whole-cell activity works through another target.

title: No Rank Correlation on the True PTP1B Active Site: A Centre-Audited Re-Dock of Four ChEMBL Leads Against Ertiprotafib on 2F71, After the Pipeline Docked the Wrong Protein
abstract: Type 2 diabetes affected 589 million adults worldwide in 2024, and Pakistan carries the world's highest age-standardised prevalence at 31.4%, yet no PTP1B inhibitor has ever been approved: the target is validated — PTP1B dephosphorylates the insulin receptor — but the only two inhibitors to reach trials, ertiprotafib and trodusquemine, both failed, and ertiprotafib was later shown to work by aggregating PTP1B rather than inhibiting it. The gap this paper attacks is whether a standardised docking screen can rank PTP1B ligands at all. We ran the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P18031 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL335, 36 bioactivities → PubChem → RDKit ADMET/PAINS → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7). The first docking run was invalid and is discarded here: the pipeline's structure picker chose 9C66, the MENA EVH1 domain, in which PTP1B appears only as a short peptide, and centred the grid on a modified cysteine of the wrong protein. The corrected re-dock placed the identical ligand set on 2F71, the PTP1B catalytic domain at 1.55 Å with a sulfamic acid inhibitor bound, the grid centre audited to the inhibitor centroid and its nearest atom 3.39 Å from the catalytic Cys215. Three leads out-scored ertiprotafib — CHEMBL5085615 −8.60, CHEMBL541214 −8.39, CHEMBL244563 −8.27 versus ertiprotafib −7.68 kcal/mol — but the margins (0.59–0.92 kcal/mol) sit inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and the ranking shows no correlation with measured potency (Spearman ρ = 0.0, n = 4), with the most potent measured binder (CHEMBL244563, Ki 0.68 nM) ranking third by Vina. The falsifiable next step is a PTP1B enzyme assay of the four leads against ertiprotafib with a TCPTP counter-screen: if the measured order matches the ChEMBL record rather than the Vina order, docking alone must not be used to prioritise PTP1B leads on this structure.

title: Vina Ranks the Most Potent KRAS G12C Binders Last: A Centre-Audited Benchmark of Sotorasib, Adagrasib, Divarasib and Two Sub-Nanomolar ChEMBL Leads on 6OIM
abstract: KRAS G12C was the first "undruggable" oncogene to fall: the covalent switch-II pocket inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib are FDA-approved, and divarasib is in Phase I, yet acquired resistance — most often the Y96D switch-II pocket mutation — limits their benefit, and the field still ranks new candidates with non-covalent docking scores. We asked whether standardised AutoDock Vina docking on the verified KRAS G12C structure 6OIM (1.65 Å, KRAS G12C covalently bound to sotorasib) can rank five covalent inhibitors by measured potency. The LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P01116, ChEMBL, PubChem, RDKit ADMET and PAINS screen, Vina 1.2.7) failed twice at target resolution — once returning zero bioactivities, once resolving KRAS to the wrong target, maltase-glucoamylase (CHEMBL2074) — so the lead set was rebuilt by direct verified queries against the correct ChEMBL target CHEMBL2189121 (4,666 activities at pChEMBL ≥ 5) plus PubChem verification of the three clinical drugs. On 6OIM, with the grid centre exactly on the co-crystallised sotorasib, Vina scored sotorasib −8.14, divarasib −8.06, adagrasib −7.58, CHEMBL4855521 −6.03 and CHEMBL4856277 −5.51 kcal/mol. The two ChEMBL leads carry the strongest measured potencies in the set — IC50 0.51 and 0.56 nM on the exact crystallised construct (KRAS G12C/C51S/C80L/C118S) — yet score worst, 2.11–2.63 kcal/mol behind sotorasib, a margin above Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise. As a control, sotorasib scored −7.22 on wild-type KRAS-GDP (9IAY), which has no cysteine-12 to bind: Vina cannot see the covalent selectivity that makes the drug work. The falsifiable next step is a covalent-aware re-scoring of the same five compounds plus a same-plate biochemical assay on the 6OIM construct: if covalent docking does not restore the measured order, non-covalent scoring should be retired as a ranking tool for this target class.

title: The Weakest Measured Binder Docks Best on CDK6: A Centre-Audited Benchmark of Four ChEMBL Leads Against Palbociclib on 6OQO
abstract: Breast cancer was diagnosed in 2.43 million women and killed 693,660 in 2024, and palbociclib — a CDK4/6 inhibitor that extended median progression-free survival in the PALOMA-2 trial — is limited by neutropenia and by resistance, so a better CDK6 binder would matter. The gap this paper attacks is whether a standardised docking screen can rank CDK6 ligands at all when the reference drug itself is the benchmark. We ran the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q00534 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL2508, 25 bioactivities → PubChem → RDKit ADMET/PAINS → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7) and docked four ChEMBL CDK6 actives plus palbociclib into the 1.98 Å CDK6 structure 6OQO, with the grid centre audited to 0.005 Å from the co-crystallised inhibitor CPD24. One lead out-scored palbociclib — CHEMBL3237704 −11.18 versus palbociclib −10.19 kcal/mol — but the margin (0.99 kcal/mol) sits inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and the ranking does not track measured potency: the most potent measured binder (CHEMBL5280928, Ki 0.2 nM) ranks third by Vina while the weakest (CHEMBL3237704, IC50 1.1 nM) ranks first, Spearman ρ = −0.32 (n = 4, p = 0.68). Palbociclib itself docked reproducibly across four independent runs (−10.20 to −10.09 kcal/mol, range 0.11). The falsifiable next step is a CDK6 kinase inhibition assay of the four leads against palbociclib with a CDK4 counter-screen: if the measured order matches the ChEMBL record rather than the Vina order, docking alone must not be used to prioritise CDK6 leads on this structure.
summary: Breast cancer was diagnosed in 2.43 million women and killed 693,660 in 2024, and palbociclib — a CDK4/6 inhibitor that extended median progression-free survival in the PALOMA-2 trial — is limited by neutropenia and by resistance, so a better CDK6 binder would matter.

title: Four Sub-Nanomolar Androgen Receptor Ligands Dock in Exact Measured-Potency Order on 8E1A — While Enzalutamide Itself Fails to Dock
abstract: Prostate cancer accounted for about 7.5% of all new cancers worldwide in 2024, roughly 1.5 million cases, and enzalutamide — an androgen receptor (AR) antagonist that extended median overall survival from 13.6 to 18.4 months in the AFFIRM trial — eventually fails in most men with metastatic castration-resistant disease, in part because the F876L ligand-binding-domain mutation converts the drug from antagonist to agonist. The gap this paper attacks is whether a standardised docking screen can rank AR ligands at all when the reference drug itself is the hard case. We ran the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P10275 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL1871, 38 bioactivities → PubChem → RDKit ADMET/PAINS → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7) and docked four ChEMBL AR actives plus enzalutamide into the 1.2 Å AR ligand-binding-domain structure 8E1A, with the grid centre audited to 0.005 Å from the co-crystallised ligand. The four leads docked in exact measured-potency order — CHEMBL391548 −9.88 kcal/mol (IC50 0.02 nM), CHEMBL3818706 −8.47 (EC50 0.032 nM), CHEMBL3819048 −8.07 (EC50 0.16 nM), CHEMBL3819648 −6.96 (EC50 0.20 nM), Spearman ρ = 1.0 — but enzalutamide itself failed to dock, scoring +0.71 kcal/mol across all three poses, and a re-dock at exhaustiveness 32 returned the same failure (+0.69 kcal/mol), ruling out search depth as the cause; a fifth lead produced no docking result at all. No "beats enzalutamide" claim can therefore be made from this screen, and no F876L-mutant structure was docked, so the resistance question the topic posed remains untested. The falsifiable next step is an AR transactivation assay of the four leads against enzalutamide in wild-type and F876L AR: if the measured antagonist order matches the ChEMBL record rather than the Vina order, docking alone must not be used to prioritise AR leads on this structure.

title: Vina Ranks Lisinopril Last on ACE: A Centre-Audited Benchmark of Enalaprilat and Two ChEMBL Leads Against Lisinopril on the C-Domain Structure 6H5W
abstract: Hypertension affected 1.4 billion people in 2024 and only about one in five had it controlled, yet the most prescribed drug class for it — ACE inhibitors — makes 5–15% of patients cough, because the same enzyme that converts angiotensin I also degrades bradykinin, and blocking it lets bradykinin accumulate in the airways. The gap this paper attacks is whether a standardised docking screen can find a better ACE binder than lisinopril, and whether that question is even the right one for a cough-free drug. We ran the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P12821 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL1808, 45 bioactivities → PubChem → RDKit ADMET/PAINS → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7) and docked four ChEMBL ACE actives plus lisinopril into the 1.37 Å ACE C-domain structure 6H5W, with the grid centre audited to 0.005 Å from the co-crystallised inhibitor omapatrilat. All four leads out-scored lisinopril — CHEMBL80779 −8.86, enalaprilat −8.15 and −8.05 (duplicate ChEMBL records of one molecule), lisinopril's own ChEMBL record −7.88, against the PubChem lisinopril query at −7.62 kcal/mol — but the ranking is inverted against measured potency: lisinopril itself, the most potent measured binder at IC50 0.1 nM, docks worst, Spearman ρ = −0.5 on the three distinct molecules. Two reproducibility controls held: lisinopril docked twice 0.26 kcal/mol apart and enalaprilat twice 0.10 apart. The cough question is not answered by binding at all: bradykinin is cleaved by both ACE domains while angiotensin I is mainly cleaved by the C-domain, so a cough-sparing inhibitor must be C-domain-selective, which a single-domain docking score cannot measure. The falsifiable next step is a two-domain (N versus C) inhibition assay of the leads against lisinopril: if a lead inhibits the C-domain while sparing the N-domain, it is a candidate for the cough question; if it inhibits both like lisinopril, it is not, whatever its docking score.

title: Black-Hole Spectroscopy at Both Ends of the Mass Ladder: GW250114's Ringdown and the First Pulsar-Timing Limits on Supermassive Binaries at Cosmic Dawn
abstract: Two results published within days of each other in November 2026 bracket the black-hole mass spectrum from opposite ends. At the stellar-mass end, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration's black-hole spectroscopy of GW250114 — the loudest gravitational-wave signal recorded to date, network signal-to-noise ratio 76 — requires at least two quasi-normal modes in the ringdown, constrains the dominant quadrupolar mode and its first overtone to match the Kerr prediction to tens of percent, and bounds the quadrupolar frequency to within a few percent of general relativity, delivering the most stringent single-event test of general relativity to date. At the supermassive end, the Parkes Pulsar Timing Array Collaboration reports the first direct nanohertz gravitational-wave limits on supermassive black-hole binaries at cosmic dawn (Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 191401, 2 November 2026), with a best all-sky chirp-mass upper limit of 8.47 × 10^9 solar masses and sensitivity mapped to redshift ~20 after correcting for a redshift bias earlier work ignored. We combine the two results into a single quantitative test. Treating the 1.2 × 10^10 solar-mass black hole in the quasar J0100+2802 (z = 6.327) as a hypothetical equal-mass binary gives a chirp mass of 5.22 × 10^9 solar masses — a factor of 1.62 below the current best pulsar-timing limit and a factor of 1.91 below the ~10^10 solar-mass exclusion quoted for that source, matching the published statement that the limits come within a factor of ~2 of the quasar's mass. A chirp-mass sensitivity improvement of a factor of ~1.6, equivalent to a factor of ~2.2 in strain, would therefore cross the threshold for this source. We state this as a falsifiable claim: if J0100+2802 assembled through a recent equal-mass merger, combined International Pulsar Timing Array data and Square Kilometre Array-era timing will detect its nanohertz signal or exclude the equal-mass binary configuration; a continued null at that sensitivity rules out the equal-mass merger origin and favours heavy-seed direct collapse or super-Eddington accretion. title: The Best Docking Score Is the Weakest Measured Binder: A Centre-Audited PPAR-gamma Screen Against Pioglitazone on 9F7W, with a Corrected ChEMBL Target
abstract: Type 2 diabetes affects 589 million adults worldwide, and Pakistan carries the world's highest age-standardised prevalence at 31.4%, yet the most effective insulin sensitiser, pioglitazone, is limited by PPAR-gamma-driven weight gain of about 3.5 kg over six months and oedema in about 5% of patients. The gap this paper attacks is whether a standardised docking screen can rank partial-agonist candidates against pioglitazone at all, and whether thymoquinone, a natural product with reported PPAR-gamma activity, binds the receptor at all. We ran the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P37231 → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit ADMET/PAINS → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7) and docked four ChEMBL PPAR-gamma actives, pioglitazone and thymoquinone into the 1.25 Å PPAR-gamma ligand-binding-domain structure 9F7W, with the grid centre audited to 0.01 Å from the co-crystallised ligand. The first pipeline run silently retrieved maltase-glucoamylase actives instead of PPAR-gamma actives; the audit caught it, and the run was repeated against the verified target CHEMBL235. One lead out-scored pioglitazone — CHEMBL6145236 at −10.24 versus −9.00 kcal/mol — but the margin (1.24 kcal/mol) sits at the edge of the ±1–2 kcal/mol Vina noise, and the ranking is reversed against measured potency: Spearman ρ = −0.8 (n = 4), with the strongest measured binder (CHEMBL1813011, EC50 0.018 nM) ranking third by Vina. Thymoquinone docked weakly (−6.25 kcal/mol) and carries a PAINS quinone alert. The falsifiable next step is a PPAR-gamma transactivation assay of the four leads against pioglitazone: if the measured EC50 order matches the ChEMBL record rather than the Vina order, docking alone must not be used to prioritise PPAR-gamma leads on this structure.
summary: Type 2 diabetes affects 589 million adults worldwide, and Pakistan carries the world's highest age-standardised prevalence at 31.4%, yet the most effective insulin sensitiser, pioglitazone, is limited by PPAR-gamma-driven weight gain of about 3.5 kg over six months and oedema in about 5% of patients.

title: No Structure to Dock On: A ChEMBL Potency Analysis of PfATP4 Inhibitors Against Cipargamin, and Why the Best Number Is a 3D7-Only Number
abstract: Malaria caused an estimated 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths in 2024, and partial artemisinin resistance is now confirmed or suspected in at least eight African countries, so a drug with a new mechanism is no longer optional. Cipargamin (KAE609), a spiroindolone that inhibits the parasite sodium pump PfATP4, cleared parasites in a median of 8 hours versus 24 hours for artemether-lumefantrine in a phase II trial, but day-28 cure was only just over 65% and the PfATP4 G358S mutation appeared in 65% of treatment failures, so the next PfATP4 drug must beat cipargamin on resistance, not on speed. We ran the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB A0A143ZZK9, corrected ChEMBL target CHEMBL6066156, 26 bioactivities across 7 compounds, PubChem verification of cipargamin, RDKit ADMET and PAINS screen) and analysed the four PfATP4 actives with measured potency against cipargamin, with docking deliberately SKIPPED because no X-ray structure of PfATP4 exists. The best record is a dihydroquinazolinone S-enantiomer at EC50 4.6 nM on the 3D7 strain, against cipargamin's literature IC50 of 0.5 to 1.4 nM, but the same compound collapses to 4,100 nM on the Dd2 strain and 7,500 nM on the G358S mutant, while its R-enantiomer holds 18.2, 26.4 and 81.3 nM across the same three assays, and two N-acetamide indoles score 150 and 790 nM with PAINS alerts. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head Na+-ATPase assay of the two enantiomers plus cipargamin on 3D7, Dd2 and G358S membrane preparations on the same plate: a lead only matters if it keeps potency where the S-enantiomer loses it.
summary: Malaria caused an estimated 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths in 2024, and partial artemisinin resistance is now confirmed or suspected in at least eight African countries, so a drug with a new mechanism is no longer optional.

title: Midostaurin Out-Docks Gilteritinib by 2.59 kcal/mol and Loses by 8-Fold in Measured Affinity: A Centre-Audited Vina Benchmark of FLT3 Inhibitors on 6JQR
abstract: FLT3 internal tandem duplication (FLT3-ITD) occurs in about 25% of acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) and confers poor prognosis with high relapse rates, yet gilteritinib, the FLT3 inhibitor with a proven survival benefit in relapsed or refractory disease, extends median overall survival to only 9.3 months, and gatekeeper (F691L) and activation-loop (D835) mutations erode even that benefit. The gap this paper attacks is whether a standardised docking screen can rank FLT3 inhibitors against gilteritinib at all. We docked gilteritinib, four established FLT3 inhibitors and seven PubChem analogues on the 2.20 Å gilteritinib-bound FLT3 kinase-domain structure 6JQR (AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, grid centred on the co-crystallised ligand centroid), after the ChEMBL activity endpoint returned HTTP 500 and the pipeline retrieved no ligands. Midostaurin scored best (−10.42 kcal/mol) and crenolanib second (−9.55), ahead of gilteritinib (−7.83) and quizartinib (−7.70), but against single-assay measured Kd values the ranking is uncorrelated (Spearman ρ = −0.3, p = 0.62, n = 5): midostaurin, the best by Vina, is the weakest measured binder (Kd 7.9 nM), while crenolanib, the strongest measured binder (Kd 0.28 nM), ranks second. Among the three type I inhibitors the reversal is exact (ρ = −1.0), so the failure is not a type I versus type II artefact. One PAINS-clean analogue (PubChem CID 150967523, −8.91 kcal/mol) out-scored gilteritinib by 1.08 kcal/mol, inside the ±1–2 kcal/mol Vina noise, and gilteritinib itself carries a PAINS alert, so neither is a lead claim. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay FLT3 kinase panel of the five inhibitors plus the three best analogues, with F691L and D835Y mutant arms: if the measured order follows the published Kd order rather than the Vina order, rigid docking must not be used to prioritise FLT3 leads on this structure.

title: No Approved Dengue Drug, No Docking Winner: NSC135618 and ARDP0006 Are Indistinguishable by Vina on the DENV NS2B–NS3 Protease Allosteric and Active-Site Structures
abstract: Dengue infected a record 14.6 million people reported to the World Health Organization in 2024, with more than 12,000 deaths, and there is still no approved antiviral drug: care is supportive only, and the single WHO-prequalified vaccine is licensed for narrow age groups in high-transmission settings. The viral NS2B-NS3 protease is the most studied dengue drug target, yet its two best-characterised published inhibitors were measured in assays that cannot be compared head-to-head: the allosteric inhibitor NSC135618 inhibits the DENV-2 protease with an IC50 of 1.8 micromolar, while the anthraquinone ARDP0006 was reported by cell-based titre reduction of more than 1 log PFU per millilitre at 1 micromolar. We asked whether standardised docking can rank them. The LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P29990, PubChem verification, RDKit ADMET and PAINS screen, AutoDock Vina 1.2.7) returned no ChEMBL lead set for this target, and its automatic structure pick was an NS1 complex, not the protease, so that score was discarded. We re-docked both inhibitors on two verified protease structures with grid centres exactly on the co-crystallised ligands: the allosteric structure 6MO2 (2.8 angstrom) and the closed active-site structure 3U1I (2.3 angstrom). On 6MO2, ARDP0006 scored minus 7.40 and NSC135618 minus 7.21 kilocalories per mole; on 3U1I, NSC135618 scored minus 6.84 and ARDP0006 minus 6.27. Every margin is under 1 kilocalorie per mole, inside Vina's plus-minus 1 to 2 kilocalorie per mole noise, and NSC135618 carries a PAINS alert from its azo group, so neither compound can be called better than the other by docking. The falsifiable next step is a single head-to-head DENV-2 protease inhibition assay for both compounds on the same plate, with redox and aggregation controls for the azo scaffold: if NSC135618's measured IC50 does not reproduce under those controls, its published potency is an artefact, not a lead.
summary: Dengue infected a record 14.6 million people reported to the World Health Organization in 2024, with more than 12,000 deaths, and there is still no approved antiviral drug: care is supportive only, and the single WHO-prequalified vaccine is licensed for narrow age groups in high-transmission settings.

title: Vina Ranks the Proven Inhibitor Last: A Centre-Audited Benchmark of 6-Methylidene Penem Inhibitors Against Enterobacter cloacae AmpC on 1RGZ Versus the Hydrolysed Substrate Ceftazidime
abstract: Third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales are a critical-priority pathogen on the WHO 2024 Bacterial Priority Pathogens List, and their inducible chromosomal AmpC beta-lactamase hydrolyses ceftazidime and related cephalosporins, so resistance can emerge during treatment itself. The gap this paper attacks is whether standardised docking can rank AmpC inhibitors at all, given that the reference drug is a substrate, not an inhibitor. We ran the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P05364 to ChEMBL CHEMBL2725, 732 bioactivities, to RDKit ADMET and PAINS screening, to AutoDock Vina 1.2.7) and docked the five most potent ChEMBL AmpC actives, 6-methylidene penems with measured IC50 values of 1 to 2 nM, plus ceftazidime and the clinically proven covalent inhibitor avibactam, into the 1.37 angstrom Enterobacter cloacae GC1 AmpC structure 1RGZ, with the grid centre exactly on the co-crystallised transition-state analogue (0.00 angstrom). Two penems out-scored ceftazidime (CHEMBL222758 minus 8.99 and CHEMBL222375 minus 8.86 versus ceftazidime minus 8.20 kcal/mol), but both margins sit inside the plus-minus 1 to 2 kcal/mol Vina noise, and the rank correlation with measured potency is weak (Spearman rho plus 0.38, n equals 5). The decisive result is avibactam: the only clinically validated AmpC inhibitor in the set scored weakest of all (minus 5.82 kcal/mol), below even the hydrolysed substrate, because its potency comes from reversible covalent carbamylation of Ser64, which non-covalent docking cannot score. The falsifiable next step is a nitrocefin hydrolysis assay of the five penems with avibactam as control: if the measured IC50 order follows the ChEMBL record rather than the Vina order, rigid docking must not be used to prioritise AmpC inhibitors.
summary: Third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales are a critical-priority pathogen on the WHO 2024 Bacterial Priority Pathogens List, and their inducible chromosomal AmpC beta-lactamase hydrolyses ceftazidime and related cephalosporins, so resistance can emerge during treatment itself.

title: Vina Ranks the Weakest Binder First: A Centre-Audited Benchmark of VEGFR2 Inhibitors on 2XIR Shows Docking Scores Do Not Recover the Measured Potency Order Against Sorafenib
abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (VEGFR2) drives tumour angiogenesis, and sorafenib — a multi-kinase inhibitor approved for hepatocellular carcinoma — blocks it with a measured VEGFR2 IC50 of 90 nM, but at the cost of promiscuous kinase inhibition and dose-limiting toxicity. The gap this paper attacks is whether a standardised docking screen can rank new VEGFR2 scaffolds against sorafenib at all. We ran the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P35968 → ChEMBL CHEMBL279, 37 bioactivities → PubChem verification → RDKit ADMET/PAINS → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7) and docked the top leads plus sorafenib into the 1.50 Å VEGFR2 kinase-domain structure 2XIR, with the grid centre exactly on the co-crystallised ligand centroid (0.00 Å). Three ChEMBL leads out-scored sorafenib — CHEMBL3586072 −11.93, CHEMBL5186748 −11.43 and CHEMBL1254007 −11.28 kcal/mol versus sorafenib −11.16 — but every margin (0.12–0.77 kcal/mol) sits inside the ±1–2 kcal/mol Vina noise, and the ranking is exactly reversed against measured potency: Spearman ρ = −1.0 (n = 4 distinct molecules), with sorafenib the strongest measured binder (pChEMBL 10.68) yet the weakest by Vina. A duplicate dock of sorafenib's own ChEMBL record (CHEMBL1336) reproduced the reference score to 0.01 kcal/mol, so the failure is in the scoring, not the setup. The falsifiable next step is a VEGFR2 kinase inhibition assay on the three leads with sorafenib as control: if the measured IC50 order matches the ChEMBL record rather than the Vina order, docking alone must not be used to prioritise VEGFR2 leads on this structure.
summary: Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (VEGFR2) drives tumour angiogenesis, and sorafenib — a multi-kinase inhibitor approved for hepatocellular carcinoma — blocks it with a measured VEGFR2 IC50 of 90 nM, but at the cost of promiscuous kinase inhibition and dose-limiting toxicity.

title: Potency Is Solved, Selectivity Is Not: A Centre-Audited PDE5 Benchmark on 1TBF, Sildenafil as the Outlier, and the PDE6 Question
abstract: Phosphodiesterase 5 (PDE5) inhibition raises cGMP and relaxes smooth muscle — the mechanism behind sildenafil for erectile dysfunction and for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), a rare disease (about 15–60 cases per million) in which untreated patients historically survived under three years. Sildenafil is potent on PDE5 (IC50 3.5 nM) but only about 10-fold selective over retinal PDE6, which is why visual disturbance is its signature side effect. The gap this paper attacks is whether a standardised docking screen can rank PDE5 leads against sildenafil, and whether potency is even the right endpoint. We ran the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB O76074 → ChEMBL CHEMBL1827, 55 bioactivities → PubChem verification → RDKit ADMET/PAINS → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7) and docked the top leads plus sildenafil into the 1.30 Å PDE5A catalytic-domain structure 1TBF, with the grid centre exactly on the co-crystallised sildenafil centroid (0.00 Å). A sulfoximine vardenafil analogue, CHEMBL4759667, led on both measures — Vina −9.71 kcal/mol and the highest measured potency (pChEMBL 10.60, IC50 0.025 nM) — but the overall rank correlation is weak (Spearman ρ = +0.30, n = 5), because sildenafil ranks second by Vina (−9.35) yet last by measured potency (pChEMBL 9.00). All five compounds are sub-nanomolar by measurement, so potency is solved; the unmet need is PDE6 selectivity, which a PDE5-only docking score cannot assess. The falsifiable next step is a paired PDE5/PDE6 inhibition assay for CHEMBL4759667 against sildenafil and vardenafil: the lead only matters if its PDE5/PDE6 selectivity ratio exceeds sildenafil's ~10-fold.
summary: Phosphodiesterase 5 (PDE5) inhibition raises cGMP and relaxes smooth muscle — the mechanism behind sildenafil for erectile dysfunction and for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), a rare disease (about 15–60 cases per million) in which untreated patients historically survived under three years.

title: No Structure to Dock On: A ChEMBL Potency Analysis of HIV-1 Integrase Inhibitors Against Dolutegravir, and Why Wild-Type Potency Is Solved but Mutant Coverage Is Not
abstract: HIV-1 infects 40.8 million people worldwide, with 1.3 million new infections and 630,000 AIDS-related deaths in 2024; in Pakistan an estimated 350,000 people live with HIV, new infections rose 200% between 2010 and 2024, and only 21% of those infected know their status. Dolutegravir, a second-generation integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI), is the backbone of first-line antiretroviral therapy because of its potency (strand-transfer IC50 2.7 nM) and high genetic barrier — but resistance through G140S/Q148H, G118R, N155H and R263K is now documented, including in 4.8% of people failing dolutegravir-based therapy in a 2026 Taiwan cohort. The gap this paper attacks is whether the next INSTI should be chosen on wild-type potency at all. We ran the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P04585 → corrected ChEMBL target CHEMBL3471, 48 bioactivities → PubChem verification → RDKit ADMET/PAINS) and analysed the top leads against dolutegravir — with docking deliberately SKIPPED, because no X-ray structure of HIV-1 integrase with a strand-transfer inhibitor exists and the pipeline's default structure pick was the wrong enzyme (HIV-1 protease, PDB 6DV4). All ten top leads are sub-3 nM by their best ChEMBL record: cabotegravir is the most potent (IC50 0.22 nM, pChEMBL 9.66), dolutegravir's own record is 0.5 nM, and seven BMS-707035-series analogues share EC50 2.0 nM in the same assay — yet the pipeline's composite score still ranks by similarity to dolutegravir, not by potency, so a different chemotype with equal potency scores far lower. Wild-type potency is solved; the falsifiable next step is a strand-transfer assay of the top leads on wild-type versus G140S/Q148H intasomes, with the investigational compound 4d as comparator: a lead only matters if it keeps potency where dolutegravir loses it.
summary: HIV-1 infects 40.8 million people worldwide, with 1.3 million new infections and 630,000 AIDS-related deaths in 2024; in Pakistan an estimated 350,000 people live with HIV, new infections rose 200% between 2010 and 2024, and only 21% of those infected know their status.

title: Sitagliptin Is the Weakest Compound in Its Own Benchmark: A Centre-Audited DPP-4 Docking Study on 4A5S Where Vina Rank and Measured Potency Are Uncorrelated
abstract: Type 2 diabetes affects 589 million adults worldwide (1 in 9), and Pakistan has one of the highest age-standardised prevalences at 31.4% (~34.5 million adults). Sitagliptin, the first DPP-4 inhibitor (FDA-approved October 2006, IC50 18 nM), prolongs incretin action by blocking the enzyme that degrades GLP-1 and GIP — but newer triazolopiperazine analogues are ~100-fold more potent in vitro, and it is not obvious that docking can tell them apart. We ran the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P27487 → ChEMBL CHEMBL284, 47 bioactivities → PubChem verification of sitagliptin → RDKit ADMET/PAINS → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on PDB 4A5S, 1.62 Å, grid centre exactly on the co-crystallised inhibitor N7F centroid, 0.00 Å) and docked the top five compounds by composite score against sitagliptin. The most similar compound to sitagliptin (CHEMBL1203953, similarity 0.563, IC50 0.18 nM) could not be docked at all — its hydrochloride salt has two SMILES fragments, which ligand preparation rejects. Of the four that docked, the Vina order (CHEMBL5870057 −9.47, sitagliptin −8.95, CHEMBL5951803 −8.85, CHEMBL5220750 −7.88 kcal/mol) is uncorrelated with the measured-potency order (Spearman ρ = 0.0, n = 4): sitagliptin ranks second by Vina yet is ~100-fold weaker than the leads by measurement (18 nM vs 0.18–0.27 nM). Worse, the single most potent compound in the whole set (CHEMBL98869, Ki 0.082 nM, pChEMBL 10.09) was never docked, because the pipeline docks only the top five by a similarity-dominated composite score. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head enzyme assay of CHEMBL5870057 and CHEMBL5951803 against sitagliptin on DPP-4 plus a DPP-8/DPP-9/FAP selectivity panel: a lead only matters if its ~100-fold potency advantage survives the same plate — and if it keeps sitagliptin's selectivity.
summary: Type 2 diabetes affects 589 million adults worldwide (1 in 9), and Pakistan has one of the highest age-standardised prevalences at 31.4% (~34.5 million adults).

title: The Weakest Drug Scores Best: Acarbose Out-Docks Three Nanomolar Iminosugars on ntMGAM 3L4Y — and the Most Potent Lead Class Could Not Be Docked at All
abstract: Type 2 diabetes affects 589 million adults worldwide — one in nine — and Pakistan carries the world's highest age-standardised prevalence at 31.4%, with about 34.5 million adults affected. α-Glucosidase inhibitors such as acarbose blunt postprandial glucose by blocking the intestinal enzymes that finish carbohydrate digestion, but acarbose is a weak inhibitor (IC50 456–750 μM in standard assays) whose undigested carbohydrate causes flatulence in 74% of users, diarrhoea in 31% and abdominal pain in 19%. The gap this paper attacks is whether a standardised docking screen can rank better α-glucosidase leads against acarbose. We ran the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB O43451 → ChEMBL CHEMBL2074, 55 bioactivities → PubChem verification → RDKit ADMET/PAINS → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7) and docked the top leads plus acarbose into the 1.80 Å N-terminal maltase-glucoamylase structure 3L4Y, with the grid centre exactly on the co-crystallised inhibitor centroid (0.00 Å). Acarbose scored best by Vina (−6.55 kcal/mol) despite being roughly 100,000-fold weaker by measurement than the best lead, a silyl-iminosugar with Ki 2.3 nM that scored only −5.02. Among the three successfully docked leads the rank correlation is weak (Spearman ρ = +0.50, n = 3), and the fifth-ranked lead — a kotalanol-class sulfonium salt with IC50 470 nM — could not be docked at all, because the pipeline rejects multi-fragment salt SMILES. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head ntMGAM inhibition assay for the three iminosugars against acarbose: if the measured order follows the ChEMBL record rather than the Vina order, docking must not be used to prioritise α-glucosidase leads on this structure, and the salt-form kotalanol analogue must be re-tested after desalting.
summary: Type 2 diabetes affects 589 million adults worldwide — one in nine — and Pakistan carries the world's highest age-standardised prevalence at 31.4%, with about 34.5 million adults affected.

title: The Serotonin Dimmer: A Falsifiable Dip-and-Recovery Model of Visual Attention Across the First Six Weeks of SSRI Therapy
abstract: Serotonin has been known for a century as a mood chemical; its control of attention was not. Lehnert et al. (Nature Communications 2026) showed that dorsal raphe serotonin neurons act as a gain control — a "dimmer switch" — on visual attention in mice: reducing serotonin activity improved detection of a faint visual target, increasing it impaired detection. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), the most widely prescribed psychiatric drugs, raise synaptic serotonin, yet the literature on their cognitive effects is contradictory: a 2018 meta-analysis of 33 studies found modest positive effects on attention in depressed patients and no effect in non-depressed participants, a 2024 fluoxetine review found the effects inconsistent and often negative in healthy animals, and a 6-week paediatric sertraline trial found no attention harm at all. We propose that these three findings are one time-course, not three contradictions. The serotonin-dimmer model states that acute elevation of serotonergic tone transiently lowers visual-attention sensitivity, and that chronic exposure restores it to or above baseline as 5-HT1A autoreceptors desensitise — predicting a measurable dip-and-recovery in attention (d′) over the first six weeks of SSRI therapy. We specify the falsifying experiment: a prospective cohort of drug-naïve depressed adults tested on a low-contrast visual search task at baseline and on days 3, 7, 14, 28 and 42, powered at n = 32 (38 with attrition) for a medium within-subject effect. If d′ does not dip in week 1, or does not recover by week 6, the model fails. This is a hypothesis and trial-design paper, not a treatment recommendation: no human attention data under SSRI initiation are presented.
