title: Five Sub-Nanomolar Binders, No Winner: A Corrected Vina Benchmark of Small-Molecule TNF-alpha Trimer Inhibitors on 2AZ5, and Why the Biologic Reference Cannot Be Docked
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis affects about 18 million people worldwide, and TNF-alpha blockade — etanercept, a 150 kDa TNFR-Fc fusion protein approved in 1998 — remains among its most effective therapies, but biologics require injection, cost, and carry infection risk including tuberculosis reactivation. Oral small molecules that bind the TNF trimer interface (SPD304, UCB-9260) have reached only the tool-compound and early-clinical stages. We benchmarked five sub-nanomolar ChEMBL TNF binders (Ki 0.03–0.083 nM) against the trimer-interface pocket with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on PDB 2AZ5 (2.1 Å), after discarding a first run that docked them on a spin-labelled TNF monomer (5UUI) at a spin-label site — a pocket that does not exist in a monomer. On the corrected trimer structure the five leads scored −8.83 to −9.67 kcal/mol, a 0.84 kcal/mol spread inside Vina noise, with rank agreement to measured Ki of Spearman rho = 0.73 (n = 5). Etanercept, the clinical reference, cannot be docked by Vina at all: it is a 150 kDa protein, not a small molecule. The falsifiable next step is a TNF–TNFR1 binding assay plus a trimer-stability (subunit-exchange) assay comparing CHEMBL3640299 with UCB-9260, to test whether the best docking score tracks the asymmetric-trimer mechanism or only pocket fit.
summary: Rheumatoid arthritis affects about 18 million people worldwide, and TNF-alpha blockade — etanercept, a 150 kDa TNFR-Fc fusion protein approved in 1998 — remains among its most effective therapies, but biologics require injection, cost, and carry infection risk including tuberculosis reactivation.

title: Posaconazole Still Leads, and the Most Potent Measured Inhibitor Scores Worst: A Vina Benchmark of Trypanosoma cruzi CYP51 Inhibitors on 4C27 That Fails to Reproduce the Potency Order
abstract: Chagas disease affects an estimated 6–7 million people, and the only approved drugs, benznidazole and nifurtimox, cure poorly in the chronic stage. Posaconazole, a sterol 14α-demethylase (CYP51) inhibitor, looked like the answer until the CHAGASAZOL trial showed 81–92% of posaconazole-treated patients PCR-positive for Trypanosoma cruzi DNA at follow-up, versus 38% on benznidazole — so the target, not just the drug, is in question. We ran the LeadForge pipeline live on 9 November 2026 (UniProtKB Q7Z1V1 → ChEMBL CHEMBL1075110, 56 ligands → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on PDB 4C27, 1.95 Å, grid centred exactly on the co-crystallised inhibitor, 0.00 Å from its centroid). Posaconazole re-docked at −10.57 kcal/mol and no lead beat it: the best challenger, CHEMBL5189694 (measured Kd 24 nM), scored −9.40, 1.17 kcal/mol worse — inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise. The striking failure is albaconazole (CHEMBL298817): the most potent measured inhibitor in the set (IC50 1.0 nM against T. cruzi CYP51) but the worst docking score, −8.16, 2.41 kcal/mol behind posaconazole. Across the four compounds with measured values, docking rank and potency rank correlate at Spearman ρ = −0.2. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head recombinant TcCYP51 inhibition assay of albaconazole, posaconazole and CHEMBL5189694 under identical conditions, with MM-GBSA rescoring to test whether the ranking failure is a scoring artefact.
summary: Chagas disease affects an estimated 6–7 million people, and the only approved drugs, benznidazole and nifurtimox, cure poorly in the chronic stage.

title: Five DSM265 Analogues Out-Dock DSM265 on Plasmodium falciparum DHODH — and the Best-Scoring One Is Not the Best Backup: A Centre-Audited Vina Benchmark on 7L01
abstract: Plasmodium falciparum dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (PfDHODH) is the validated target of DSM265, the first DHODH inhibitor to reach clinical development for malaria. We ran the LeadForge pipeline live on 9 November 2026 (UniProtKB Q08210 → ChEMBL CHEMBL3588732, 58 ligands → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → Vina docking on PDB 7L01, grid centred on the co-crystallised DSM782 inhibitor, FMN cofactor and orotate excluded). The pipeline rediscovered DSM265 itself (CHEMBL1956285, similarity 1.000, IC50 27 nM). Five triazolopyrimidine analogues docked better than the DSM265 re-dock (−8.21 kcal/mol): CHEMBL3289670 −9.72, CHEMBL1738786 −9.58 and CHEMBL1956290 −9.33, margins of 1.12–1.51 kcal/mol that clear the 0.42 kcal/mol preparation noise but sit inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol error, so none is proven better. The most drug-like lead, CHEMBL1956283 (IC50 28 nM, MW 323.73, logP 3.94, zero Lipinski violations against DSM265's one), docked only −8.68. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head recombinant PfDHODH enzyme assay of CHEMBL3289670, CHEMBL1738786 and CHEMBL1956283 against DSM265, plus docking and assay on the C276F resistance mutant (PDB 6E0B), whose X-ray structure shows a restricted pocket.
summary: Plasmodium falciparum dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (PfDHODH) is the validated target of DSM265, the first DHODH inhibitor to reach clinical development for malaria.

title: Pyrimethamine Docks Worst on Its Own Resistant Mutant — And That Is the Correct Answer: A Vina Benchmark on Quadruple-Mutant PfDHFR-TS 1J3K
abstract: Malaria caused about 263 million cases and 597,000 deaths in 2023, and sulfadoxine–pyrimethamine — still used for intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy and seasonal chemoprevention — is compromised by point mutations in Plasmodium falciparum dihydrofolate reductase (PfDHFR): N51I, C59R, S108N and I164L, whose quadruple combination confers high-level pyrimethamine resistance. We benchmarked pyrimethamine against four sub-nanomolar ChEMBL diaminopyrimidine analogues on the quadruple-mutant enzyme (PDB 1J3K, 2.10 Å) with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, after discarding two pipeline runs that resolved the wrong target (human maltase-glucoamylase) or a sparsely annotated 3D7 record. On the mutant structure pyrimethamine docked worst (−7.48 kcal/mol; its duplicate record CHEMBL36 −7.45), behind CHEMBL21885 (−8.38), CHEMBL21778 (−7.52) and CHEMBL282275 (−7.49). Against wild-type Ki values the rank correlation is a perfect inversion (Spearman rho = −1.0, n = 4) — but the Ki values are wild-type, while the structure is mutant. Against matched S108N-mutant Ki values (pyrimethamine 71.7 nM; analogues 10.6–66.2 nM) the correlation is weakly positive (rho = 0.40) and pyrimethamine is worst in both. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head enzyme assay of all four compounds on wild-type and quadruple-mutant PfDHFR-TS under identical conditions, to test whether the docking order tracks the mutant enzyme.

title: The Only Approved Drug Scores Worst: Dorzagliatin Binds Weakest on Human Glucokinase 3F9M While Four Nanomolar Activators Lead — A Vina Benchmark That Separates Affinity from Activation
abstract: Type 2 diabetes affected 537 million adults in 2021 and is projected to reach 643 million by 2030, yet glucokinase activators (GKAs) — a mechanistically attractive class — failed repeatedly in trials through hypoglycaemia, hypertriglyceridaemia and fading efficacy, leaving dorzagliatin, approved only in China in 2022, as the sole survivor. We asked whether docking affinity at the glucokinase allosteric site explains that survival, benchmarking dorzagliatin against four nanomolar ChEMBL activators on human glucokinase (PDB 3F9M, 1.5 Å) with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 under one protocol. The approved drug scored worst: dorzagliatin −6.82 kcal/mol, against −8.47 for CHEMBL3217925 (Kd 2.16 nM), −8.25 for CHEMBL3577729, −7.85 for CHEMBL3577715 and −7.50 for CHEMBL3580737 (Kd 2.93 nM). The 1.65 kcal/mol gap to the best lead sits inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and the rank correlation between measured potency and docking score was weak (Spearman rho = 0.35, n = 4), with the second-most-potent measured binder ranking last in docking. Affinity therefore does not explain dorzagliatin's clinical success; its published advantage is glucose-dependent activation kinetics, not maximal binding. The falsifiable next step is a recombinant glucokinase activation assay at 3, 5 and 10 mmol/L glucose comparing EC50 and Vmax of CHEMBL3217925 with dorzagliatin: if the lead activates at low glucose like the failed MK-0941, affinity is a liability, not a lead.

title: No Lead Beats Novobiocin Beyond Noise on Escherichia coli GyrB: A Corrected Vina Benchmark on 7P2M and the Wrong-Site Comparator Problem
abstract: Fluoroquinolone resistance in Gram-negative bacteria is driven by mutations in the quinolone-resistance-determining region of gyrA (S83L, D87N) and parC (S80I) — the GyrA subunit and topoisomerase IV, not GyrB. The GyrB ATPase site is therefore a resistance-bypassing target, and its classic inhibitor is novobiocin. We ran the LeadForge pipeline live on 9 November 2026 (UniProtKB P0AES6 → ChEMBL CHEMBL1826, 50 ligands → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on PDB 7P2M, 1.16 Å, grid 0.01 Å from the co-crystallised inhibitor centroid). A first pipeline run resolved the wrong target (Thermus thermophilus GyrB plus human maltase-glucoamylase, CHEMBL2074) and was discarded. In the corrected run, four GyrB ATPase-domain inhibitors (measured IC50 3–8 nM) docked at −7.17 to −8.78 kcal/mol. The best, CHEMBL4293447 (−8.78), beats the true ATP-site reference novobiocin (−7.76, Kd 28 nM) by 1.02 kcal/mol — inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise — and beats ciprofloxacin (−7.26) by 1.52 kcal/mol, also inside noise. Ciprofloxacin does not bind the GyrB ATP site at all (it binds the GyrA–DNA cleavage complex), so its respectable score shows absolute Vina scores are not evidence of binding. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head E. coli GyrB ATPase assay of CHEMBL4293447, CHEMBL4294536 and novobiocin under identical conditions, plus MICs against gyrA S83L/D87N mutants to test the resistance-bypass claim directly.
summary: Fluoroquinolone resistance in Gram-negative bacteria is driven by mutations in the quinolone-resistance-determining region of gyrA (S83L, D87N) and parC (S80I) — the GyrA subunit and topoisomerase IV, not GyrB. The GyrB ATPase site is therefore a resistance-bypassing target, and its classic inhibitor is novobiocin.

title: Two Furoxan Analogues Out-Dock Praziquantel on Schistosoma TGR — But Praziquantel Does Not Target TGR: A Corrected Vina Benchmark on 8PDD
abstract: Schistosomiasis required preventive treatment for at least 253.7 million people in 2024, yet only 39.6% of them were reached, and control still rests on a single drug, praziquantel, which kills adult worms but not eggs or immature worms and does not prevent reinfection. Thioredoxin glutathione reductase (TGR) of Schistosoma mansoni is a selenocysteine flavoenzyme that is the parasite's sole route for both thioredoxin and glutathione reduction — a validated drug target with no human equivalent. We ran the LeadForge pipeline live on 8 November 2026 (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → Vina docking) against the 1.25 Å SmTGR structure (PDB 8PDD), docking praziquantel plus five known TGR inhibitors (measured potencies 10–100 nM) with an identical AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 protocol. Two furoxan (oxadiazole 2-oxide) analogues out-docked praziquantel: CHEMBL3322292 (IC50 83 nM) at −10.93 kcal/mol and CHEMBL3322287 (IC50 10 nM) at −10.27 kcal/mol, against praziquantel at −9.59 kcal/mol — but praziquantel does not act on TGR, so beating it on this site is a cross-docking control, not a therapeutic comparison, and the docking order inverts the measured potencies (the 83 nM compound docks better than the 10 nM compound by 0.66 kcal/mol). The grid centre was corrected during the run: the first attempt centred on the FAD cofactor, and re-docking at the redox-active cysteine site changed no ranking and shifted scores by at most 0.66 kcal/mol, showing the conclusion is robust to that error. The falsifiable next step is a TGR enzyme assay of the two furoxans head-to-head with a pre-registered rule that a docking margin under 2 kcal/mol predicts no measurable potency advantage; a furoxan that inhibits TGR at its ChEMBL IC50 and kills schistosomula would refute the claim that docking order on this target is uninformative.
summary: Schistosomiasis required preventive treatment for at least 253.7 million people in 2024, yet only 39.6% of them were reached, and control still rests on a single drug, praziquantel, which kills adult worms but not eggs or immature worms and does not prevent reinfection.

title: Three Diazabicyclooctanes "Beat" Avibactam by Docking and Lose by Less Than 1 kcal/mol of Noise: A Vina Benchmark of KPC-2 Inhibitors on 6TD0 — and the Boronate Blind Spot
abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase (KPC-2) is the most commonly encountered class A beta-lactamase variant worldwide, and it confers high-level resistance to most available antibiotics; ceftazidime-avibactam is the standard inhibitor combination against it, but omega-loop variants such as D179N already escape it. We ran the LeadForge pipeline live on 8 November 2026 (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → Vina docking): target KPC-2 (UniProt Q9F663, ChEMBL CHEMBL6132, 4 bioactivities retrieved), structure PDB 6TD0 at 0.99 angstrom, grid centred exactly on the co-crystallised vaborbactam (centroid [15.45, 8.23, 21.26]), and six ligands docked with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 under an identical protocol. Nacubactam scored −7.65 kcal/mol, a 2-sulfamoyl diazabicyclooctane −7.50 and relebactam −7.35, against avibactam at −6.73 (re-dock −7.15) and tazobactam at −6.42 — margins of 0.62–0.92 kcal/mol, all inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, so no compound can be called better than avibactam on these scores. Two clinically important boronates, vaborbactam and taniborbactam, could not be docked at all: the pipeline writes boron as PDBQT atom type "B", which this Vina build rejects, and their covalent boron–Ser70 mechanism is outside non-covalent docking in any case. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head KPC-2 inhibition assay (nitrocefin hydrolysis, purified enzyme, same plate) of nacubactam and relebactam against avibactam, with a pre-registered rule that a docking margin under 2 kcal/mol predicts no measurable Ki advantage; a measured Ki for nacubactam tighter than avibactam's would refute the noise interpretation, and re-running the same benchmark on the D179N variant structure (PDB 8G2R) would test whether the ranking survives the resistance mutation.
summary: Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase (KPC-2) is the most commonly encountered class A beta-lactamase variant worldwide, and it confers high-level resistance to most available antibiotics; ceftazidime-avibactam is the standard inhibitor combination against it, but omega-loop variants such as D179N already escape it.

title: Oseltamivir Scores Worst on Its Own Wildtype Site — and Better on the Resistant Mutant: A Vina Benchmark on 3TI6 and 3CL0 That Fails to Reproduce H274Y Resistance
abstract: Seasonal influenza infects about a billion people a year and causes 290,000–650,000 respiratory deaths, and oseltamivir is the first-line antiviral — yet the H274Y neuraminidase mutation, which swept to more than 90% of seasonal H1N1 in 2008–09, makes the virus resistant to it by shifting the Glu276 side chain into the drug's hydrophobic pocket. We ran the LeadForge pipeline live on 8 November 2026 (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → Vina docking) against the 2009 pandemic H1N1 neuraminidase (PDB 3TI6) and its H274Y mutant (PDB 3CL0), docking oseltamivir plus five oseltamivir-scaffold analogues with measured IC50 values of 0.3–1.8 nM, each centred on the co-crystallised oseltamivir, under an identical AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 protocol. The protocol fails the test it was built for: oseltamivir scores worst of all six ligands on the wildtype site (−4.83 kcal/mol), every ligand scores better on the resistant mutant than on the wildtype (oseltamivir −6.48 vs −4.83 kcal/mol), and the docking order disagrees with measured potency on both structures. The falsifiable next step is a neuraminidase inhibition assay of the best-docking analogue against oseltamivir on wildtype and H274Y enzymes, with a pre-registered rule that a docking margin under 2 kcal/mol predicts no measurable advantage; an analogue that inhibits the H274Y enzyme at its ChEMBL IC50 would refute the claim that rigid docking on a drug-bound mutant structure cannot reproduce resistance.

title: No Statin Beats Atorvastatin Beyond Noise: A Vina Benchmark of Four HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitors on 2R4F, and the Non-Statin Scaffold the Screen Did Not Find
abstract: Cardiovascular disease killed about 19.8 million people in 2022, a third of all deaths, and high LDL cholesterol is one of its main modifiable drivers. Atorvastatin blocks HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis, and each 1 mmol/L of LDL lowering cuts major vascular events by about a fifth — but muscle symptoms make some patients stop statins, and the SAMSON trial showed about 90% of those symptoms are also felt on placebo, so true statin intolerance is uncommon (about 3–5%) yet real, and non-statin alternatives are still needed. We ran the LeadForge pipeline live on 8 November 2026 (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → Vina docking) against the human HMG-CoA reductase structure in complex with a pyrazole inhibitor (PDB 2R4F), with the grid centred on the co-crystallised inhibitor, and docked atorvastatin plus four known HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors with measured IC50 values of 0.23–1.8 nM, all under an identical AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 protocol. No compound beat atorvastatin beyond noise: atorvastatin scored best at −9.00 kcal/mol, the closest lead (atorvastatin itself in ChEMBL, IC50 0.23 nM) trailed by 0.40 kcal/mol, and the most potent measured inhibitor in the set is atorvastatin itself — every margin inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and the docking order disagrees with measured potency. The screen also failed its stated purpose: all four leads are statins or statin analogues carrying the same 3,5-dihydroxyheptanoate pharmacophore, so no non-statin scaffold was tested at all. The falsifiable next step is a deliberately dissimilarity-based screen for non-statin HMG-CoA reductase binders plus an LDL-lowering assay of the best-docking lead against atorvastatin, with a pre-registered rule that a docking margin under 2 kcal/mol predicts no measurable advantage; a non-statin lead that lowers LDL in a statin-intolerant model would refute the claim that this target has nothing left to offer beyond statins.
summary: Cardiovascular disease killed about 19.8 million people in 2022, a third of all deaths, and high LDL cholesterol is one of its main modifiable drivers.

title: Daclatasvir-Class NS5A Inhibitors Are All Picomolar and All Beyond the Rule of Five: A Corrected Ligand Screen, and Why Docking Was Skipped
abstract: Pakistan carries the world's largest hepatitis C burden — about 9 million people chronically infected in 2024, about 88,000 new infections that year, and about 48,700 hepatitis deaths — and genotype 3a, the hardest genotype to cure with first-generation regimens, accounts for roughly 55–80% of Pakistani infections. Daclatasvir, the first-in-class NS5A inhibitor, blocks the viral NS5A protein at picomolar concentrations, but a single substitution, Y93H, raises its EC50 by thousands of fold, and the whole drug class is large and lipophilic. We ran the LeadForge pipeline live on 8 November 2026 (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET) against the verified hepatitis C NS5A target (ChEMBL CHEMBL3307224; 48 bioactivities) and ranked daclatasvir plus 25 known NS5A inhibitors. The top five leads are indistinguishable by potency — all EC50 0.010–0.013 nM — and indistinguishable by drug-likeness: every one carries two Lipinski violations and fails Veber's rules, exactly like daclatasvir itself. Docking was skipped, honestly and deliberately: the only NS5A domain I crystal structure (PDB 1ZH1, 2.5 Å) is apo, and no co-crystal of any daclatasvir-class inhibitor with NS5A exists, so there is no experimental binding site to dock into. The falsifiable next step is a defined docking run on 1ZH1 at the modelled dimer-interface site plus a genotype 3a replicon assay of the best-ranked lead against daclatasvir on wild-type and Y93H NS5A, with a pre-registered rule that a lead must keep picomolar potency on Y93H to count as an advance; a lead that loses potency on Y93H like daclatasvir would confirm that this class has no resistance advantage to offer.
summary: Pakistan carries the world's largest hepatitis C burden — about 9 million people chronically infected in 2024, about 88,000 new infections that year, and about 48,700 hepatitis deaths — and genotype 3a, the hardest genotype to cure with first-generation regimens, accounts for roughly 55–80% of Pakistani infections.

title: No Lead Beats Letrozole Beyond Noise: A Vina Benchmark of Five Aromatase Inhibitors on the Human CYP19A1 Structure 3S79
abstract: Breast cancer was diagnosed in about 2.4 million women in 2024 and killed about 694,000; in Pakistan it is the commonest female cancer, with about 30,682 new cases and 15,552 deaths in 2022 and the highest incidence rate in Asia. Letrozole, a third-generation aromatase inhibitor, blocks CYP19A1 aromatase, the enzyme that converts androgens to oestrogens, and in the BIG 1-98 trial it cut the risk of recurrence by 18% versus tamoxifen (hazard ratio 0.82), but bone loss, arthralgia and acquired resistance limit its benefit, so new aromatase inhibitors are still wanted. We ran the LeadForge pipeline live on 8 November 2026 (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → Vina docking) against the human aromatase structure in complex with androstenedione (PDB 3S79, 2.75 Å), with the grid centred on the co-crystallised androstenedione, and docked letrozole plus five known aromatase inhibitors with measured potencies of 0.02–0.21 nM, all under an identical AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 protocol. No lead beat letrozole beyond noise: the best lead (CHEMBL197650, IC50 0.11 nM) scored −8.77 kcal/mol against letrozole's −8.74, a 0.03 kcal/mol margin, and the most potent measured inhibitor (letrozole itself in ChEMBL, Ki 0.02 nM) scored −8.71; every margin is inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise and the docking order disagrees with measured potency. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head aromatase inhibition assay of the best-docking lead against letrozole on wild-type and resistant-mutant enzyme, with a pre-registered rule that a docking margin under 2 kcal/mol predicts no measurable advantage; a lead that keeps potency where letrozole loses it, or a measured IC50 advantage over letrozole, would refute the claim that the docking ranking is only a measurement of Vina's limits.
summary: Breast cancer was diagnosed in about 2.4 million women in 2024 and killed about 694,000; in Pakistan it is the commonest female cancer, with about 30,682 new cases and 15,552 deaths in 2022 and the highest incidence rate in Asia.

title: Multi-target computational triage of known bioactive chemical space against seven disease targets (week of 2-8 Nov 2026)
abstract: We screened the bioactive chemical space of ChEMBL against seven therapeutically relevant targets in one week of automated LeadForge runs (2–8 Nov 2026): FLT3, Plasmodium falciparum ATP4, Pseudomonas aeruginosa LpxC, acetylcholinesterase (AChE), isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1), Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) and menin (MEN1). For each target, the reference drug was recovered from live ChEMBL data (rediscovery check), 19–53 known ligands were similarity-screened, leads were ranked on a composite of similarity, Lipinski/Veber drug-likeness, PAINS and kNN toxicity read-across, and the top five leads were docked with AutoDock Vina against the best available X-ray structure, with the reference drug re-docked as control. Two runs produced leads that docked clearly better than their reference drug: CHEMBL5816906 against menin (−10.10 vs −8.37 kcal/mol for revumenib) and three scaffold-distinct leads against LpxC (best −10.85 vs −9.34 for ACHN-975). Three runs were effective ties (FLT3, AChE, IDH1) and one was an honest negative (BTK: no lead beat ibrutinib). One run (PfATP4) had no structure for docking but identified CHEMBL5591927, the strongest measured PfATP4 active in ChEMBL (EC50 4.6 nM), as a scaffold-distinct backup to cipargamin. All findings are computational triage; no compound is claimed as a drug, and wet-lab validation is required.

title: The Archive Is the Telescope: What Physics-Based PSF Subtraction Predicts for Hidden Worlds in the JWST Archive — and the Cold Census It Unlocks
abstract: Two results published in the first week of November 2026 change what existing telescope data can still deliver. First, Ferrer-Chavez et al. (2026) demonstrate Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets (FLIP), a differentiable model-based point-spread-function subtraction that improves JWST/NIRCam coronagraphic sensitivity by a factor of 2–15 over the standard KLIP pipeline and recovers 51 Eridani b at 4.3 μm, where KLIP returned a non-detection. Second, Liu et al. (2026) show that "Capotauro", a candidate galaxy at redshift $z \simeq 32$, moved by $132 \pm 20$ milliarcseconds over 3.5 years and is instead a Y1 dwarf at $\sim$350 K and $730 \pm 110$ pc — one of the most distant Y dwarfs known. We combine these results with the JADES census of 41 T- and Y-dwarf candidates in 309.5 arcmin$^2$ and the two Bullet Cluster dropouts confirmed as Y dwarfs, and we derive three quantitative, falsifiable consequences. (1) FLIP-class reprocessing of the JWST coronagraphic archive: from the single published KLIP non-detection that FLIP turned into a $6.3\sigma$ detection, the one-sided 95% lower bound on the per-dataset recovery rate is 5%; reprocessing 20 such datasets therefore has a $\ge$64% probability of at least one new companion, and 59 datasets give $>$95%. (2) The Habitable Worlds Observatory stability requirement — 100–1000 times the stability of JWST — is reduced by the measured FLIP gain to a residual gap of 6.7–500 times, i.e. from 2–3 orders of magnitude to 0.8–2.7. (3) Capotauro's proper motion, $37.6$ mas yr$^{-1}$, implies a transverse velocity of $\approx 130 \pm 20$ km s$^{-1}$ at 730 pc, consistent with thick-disc/halo kinematics and with the JADES finding that most ultra-distant candidates are metal-poor subdwarfs. We state the observing programmes that would test each claim, including a 59-dataset falsification threshold for the archive yield and a proper-motion screen for the next ultra-high-redshift dropout candidates. Keywords: exoplanets; direct imaging; JWST; PSF subtraction; brown dwarfs; Y dwarfs; high-redshift galaxies; Habitable Worlds Observatory
summary: Two results published in the first week of November 2026 change what existing telescope data can still deliver. First, Ferrer-Chavez et al.

title: Posaconazole "Beats" Four CYP51 Binders by Docking but the Target Itself Is in Doubt: A Vina Benchmark of Mycobacterium tuberculosis CYP51 on 2CIB and the Repurposing Limits of Azole Anti-TB Activity
abstract: Tuberculosis made about 10.8 million people ill in 2023 and killed about 1.25 million, and azole antifungals have shown real antimycobacterial activity — econazole and clotrimazole kill Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv at 0.12 micrograms per millilitre — yet the target usually named for that activity, the sterol 14alpha-demethylase CYP51 (Rv0764c), sits in a bacterium that makes no sterols and lacks the rest of the sterol biosynthetic pathway, so whether CYP51 inhibition explains the killing is unproven. We ran the LeadForge pipeline live on 7 November 2026 (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → Vina docking): target M. tuberculosis CYP51 (UniProt P9WPP9, ChEMBL CHEMBL5090, 12 bioactivities), structure PDB 2CIB at 1.50 angstrom, grid centred exactly on the co-crystallised inhibitor CM6 ([−16.89, −2.19, 69.32], 6.7 angstrom from the haem centroid), and five ligands docked with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 under an identical protocol. Posaconazole, the repurposed triazole comparator, scored −7.99 kcal/mol, beating every lead by 1.30–2.13 kcal/mol — fluconazole −6.44, CHEMBL521787 −6.69, CHEMBL507264 −6.64, CHEMBL491289 −5.86 — but the ranking among the leads is inverted against measured binding: fluconazole, the tightest binder by ChEMBL Kd (200 nM), scores third, behind two 5,000 nM binders, and all margins sit inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise. The decisive limit is mechanistic, not numerical: azoles inhibit CYP51 by coordinating the haem iron, an interaction Vina cannot model, and posaconazole has no measured M. tuberculosis CYP51 affinity and no anti-TB MIC at all, so its docking win cannot be read as anti-TB activity. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head CYP51 binding assay (spectral Kd) for posaconazole against fluconazole, with a pre-registered rule that a docking margin under 2 kcal/mol predicts no measurable affinity advantage; a measured posaconazole Kd tighter than fluconazole's 200 nM, or a CYP51-knockout strain that stays azole-sensitive, would refute the claim that the docking win is only a measurement of Vina's limits and of a target whose essentiality is unproven.

title: No Lead Beats Bedaquiline on Its Own Site: A Vina Benchmark of Five ATP Synthase Inhibitors on the M. tuberculosis Fo Structure 8J57
abstract: Tuberculosis made about 10.8 million people ill in 2023 and killed about 1.25 million, and Pakistan alone accounted for about 686,000 cases and 47,000 deaths. Bedaquiline, the first diarylquinoline, blocks the Mycobacterium tuberculosis ATP synthase by binding its c-ring subunit AtpE, but it carries boxed warnings for QT prolongation and increased mortality, and resistance is already emerging through atpE target mutations and mmpR5 efflux derepression. We ran the LeadForge pipeline live on 7 November 2026 (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → Vina docking) against the M. tuberculosis ATP synthase Fo structure in complex with bedaquiline (PDB 8J57, 2.85 Å cryo-EM), with the grid centred on the co-crystallised bedaquiline copy at the a–c interface, and docked bedaquiline plus five known ATP synthase inhibitors with measured on-target IC50 values of 1–70 nM, all under an identical AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 protocol. No lead beat bedaquiline: bedaquiline scored best at −8.13 kcal/mol, the closest lead (CHEMBL3754231, IC50 10 nM) trailed by 0.55 kcal/mol, and the most potent measured inhibitor (CHEMBL3754673, IC50 1 nM) scored only −7.37 kcal/mol — every margin inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and the docking order disagrees with the measured potency order. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head ATP synthesis inhibition assay of the best-docking lead against bedaquiline on wild-type and Glu61Asp AtpE enzyme, with a pre-registered rule that a docking margin under 2 kcal/mol predicts no measurable advantage; a lead that keeps potency on the Glu61Asp mutant, or a measured IC50 advantage over bedaquiline, would refute the claim that the docking ranking is only a measurement of Vina's limits.
summary: Tuberculosis made about 10.8 million people ill in 2023 and killed about 1.25 million, and Pakistan alone accounted for about 686,000 cases and 47,000 deaths.

title: Vebicorvir "Beats" Bersacapavir by Docking and Loses by 1.10 kcal/mol of Noise: A Vina Benchmark of HBV Capsid Assembly Modulators on 5WRE and the Functional-Cure Gap
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B affected about 240 million people and caused about 1.1 million deaths in 2024, yet no approved drug clears the virus: nucleos(t)ide analogues suppress replication indefinitely and functional cure — sustained hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss off treatment — remains rare. Capsid assembly modulators (CAMs) that bind the core protein dimer-dimer interface are the most advanced new mechanism, but no CAM is approved, and the most advanced, bersacapavir, reached phase 2b without a single functional cure in the REEF-2 trial. We benchmarked four CAMs against the same HBV core-protein pocket with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on PDB 5WRE (1.95 Å, HAP-bound): the investigational comparator bersacapavir, the phase 2 heteroaryldihydropyrimidine GLS4 (morphothiadin), the discontinued vebicorvir, and the co-crystallised HAP_R01 as a re-dock control. Vebicorvir scored best at −8.03 kcal/mol, beating bersacapavir (−6.93 kcal/mol) by 1.10 kcal/mol, with HAP_R01 at −6.76 and GLS4 last at −6.53 kcal/mol — but the ranking is inverted against measured potency: vebicorvir is the weakest by experiment (EC50 173–250 nM), while GLS4 is the most potent (IC50 12 nM) and bersacapavir sits between them (EC50 45 nM). The 1.10 kcal/mol margin is inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, so the docking "win" is not a discovery. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head HBV replication assay of vebicorvir against bersacapavir under identical conditions, with a pre-registered rule that a docking margin under 2 kcal/mol predicts no measurable potency advantage; a measured advantage for vebicorvir would refute the noise interpretation.
summary: Chronic hepatitis B affected about 240 million people and caused about 1.1 million deaths in 2024, yet no approved drug clears the virus: nucleos(t)ide analogues suppress replication indefinitely and functional cure — sustained hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss off treatment — remains rare.

title: No Pocket to Dock: A Negative Computational Result for Small-Molecule Targeting of BCL11A in Beta-Thalassaemia
abstract: Beta-thalassaemia affects about 5-8% of Pakistan's population as carriers, roughly 9.8 million people, with an estimated 5,000 to 9,000 children born with thalassaemia major each year, and raising fetal haemoglobin (HbF) is the best-validated way to soften the disease. BCL11A is the master repressor of the fetal gamma-globin genes, and genetic disruption of its erythroid enhancer made 91% of patients transfusion-independent in the CLIMB THAL-111 trial, yet that therapy is a one-time ex vivo gene edit far beyond the reach of most Pakistani patients, while the cheap oral HbF inducer hydroxyurea works indirectly, variably, and not by binding BCL11A. We ran the LeadForge pipeline live on 7 November 2026 (UniProtKB to ChEMBL to PubChem to RDKit to PAINS/ADMET to Vina docking) asking whether any small molecule could be docked against BCL11A as a first triage step. The pipeline correctly identified human BCL11A (UniProt Q9H165) but found zero known ligands for it in ChEMBL and only the reference drug itself, hydroxyurea, to dock. Docking did produce a number, minus 4.26 kcal/mol on PDB 8DTN, but a centre audit refutes it: the grid was centred on a single selenomethionine residue (MSE A34) of the co-crystallised nanobody, not on BCL11A and not on any binding pocket, because 8DTN contains no small-molecule ligand at all, and no ligand-bound BCL11A structure exists in the Protein Data Bank. The score is therefore discarded, docking is skipped as a method on this target, and the durable results are the negative ones: no ChEMBL ligand, no druggable pocket in any deposited structure, and a pipeline fault in which the centre picker falls back to a modified residue when no ligand exists. The falsifiable next step is a cellular assay, not more docking: a K562 or primary erythroid gamma-globin reporter screen of a focused library, with a pre-registered rule that a compound must raise gamma-globin mRNA at least two-fold without cytotoxicity, and a direct BCL11A binding test for any hit, since a docking score on this target cannot be the evidence.
summary: Beta-thalassaemia affects about 5-8% of Pakistan's population as carriers, roughly 9.8 million people, with an estimated 5,000 to 9,000 children born with thalassaemia major each year, and raising fetal haemoglobin (HbF) is the best-validated way to soften the disease.

title: Two Dietary Flavonoids "Beat" Acarbose by Docking and Lose by ~1 kcal/mol of Noise: A Vina Benchmark of Human Pancreatic Alpha-Amylase Inhibitors on 1XCX
abstract: Diabetes affected an estimated 828 million adults in 2022, including 36 million in Pakistan, where the prevalence among women rose from 9.0% in 1990 to 30.9% in 2022, the largest increase of any country, and most post-meal glucose control still depends on slowing starch digestion. Acarbose, the standard alpha-amylase and alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, blunts postprandial glucose but causes flatulence in 74% of patients, diarrhoea in 31% and abdominal pain in 19%, which limits adherence; dietary flavonoids are proposed as gentler adjuncts, but their published enzyme inhibition has rarely been benchmarked against acarbose in the same protocol. We ran the LeadForge pipeline live on 7 November 2026 (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → Vina docking): target human pancreatic alpha-amylase (UniProt P04746, AMY2A; ChEMBL CHEMBL2045, 23 bioactivities), structure PDB 1XCX at 1.9 Å, grid centred on the co-crystallised acarbose-derived ligand ([5.01, 16.45, 41.56]), and six ligands docked with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 under an identical protocol. Luteolin scored −8.42 kcal/mol and quercetin −8.31 kcal/mol against acarbose at −7.35 kcal/mol, margins of 1.07 and 0.96 kcal/mol, inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, while both flavonoids carry PAINS catechol alerts and quercetin's oral bioavailability is under 10%. A ChEMBL acarbose isomer with a measured Ki of 12 nM scored −8.14 kcal/mol, and a second analogue (Ki 75 nM) scored −7.47 kcal/mol, ranking in the same order as their measured potency. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head in vitro alpha-amylase inhibition assay of luteolin against acarbose under identical conditions with redox controls, with a pre-registered rule that a docking margin under 2 kcal/mol predicts no measurable advantage; a measured IC50 for luteolin better than acarbose's under those controls would refute the noise interpretation.
summary: Diabetes affected an estimated 828 million adults in 2022, including 36 million in Pakistan, where the prevalence among women rose from 9.0% in 1990 to 30.9% in 2022, the largest increase of any country, and most post-meal glucose control still depends on slowing starch digestion.

title: Febuxostat Beats Itself by 0.03 kcal/mol: A Vina Benchmark of Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitors on 2E1Q, and the Selenium Ligands the Pipeline Cannot Dock
abstract: Gout is driven by hyperuricaemia, and xanthine oxidase catalyses the final steps of uric-acid formation while also generating reactive oxygen species, making it the established target for urate-lowering therapy. Febuxostat, a non-purine xanthine oxidase inhibitor, is effective but carries a contested cardiovascular safety record: the FDA-mandated CARES trial found higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality with febuxostat than with allopurinol despite no difference in the primary composite endpoint, leading to a boxed warning, while the later FAST trial found no excess mortality, and a 2025 Japanese nationwide claims cohort of patients with chronic kidney disease found no significant difference in composite cardiovascular outcomes (hazard ratio 0.93). We asked whether a standardised automated docking pipeline could find a xanthine oxidase inhibitor that binds more tightly than febuxostat. The LeadForge pipeline was run live on 6 November 2026 on human xanthine dehydrogenase/oxidase (UniProt P47989, ChEMBL CHEMBL1929, 53 bioactivities); 25 compounds passed the similarity screen and 26 were ranked. Five leads were docked with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on PDB 2E1Q (2.6 Å), the grid centred exactly on the co-crystallised ligand — febuxostat itself — at [35.35, 15.17, 152.43]. No lead beats febuxostat: the best-scoring "lead", CHEMBL1164729 at −7.53 kcal/mol, is febuxostat itself entered under a second ChEMBL ID, scoring 0.03 kcal/mol from the query entry (−7.50). The best genuine lead, CHEMBL5436777 (IC50 1.0 nM), scored −7.42 kcal/mol, 0.08 kcal/mol from febuxostat — a tie inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise. Two of the five leads, both selenium-containing analogues, could not be docked at all because the pipeline cannot prepare selenium ligands. Febuxostat's own Tox21 read-across panel returns probability 1.0 on three assays, an identity artifact, not a toxicity signal. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head xanthine oxidase enzyme inhibition assay of CHEMBL5436777 against febuxostat under identical conditions, with a pre-registered rule that a docking margin under 2 kcal/mol predicts no measurable potency advantage; a measured potency advantage greater than 2-fold for CHEMBL5436777, or a successful docking of the selenium analogues after the ligand-preparation fault is fixed, would refute the claim that no lead in this set improves on febuxostat.
summary: Gout is driven by hyperuricaemia, and xanthine oxidase catalyses the final steps of uric-acid formation while also generating reactive oxygen species, making it the established target for urate-lowering therapy.

title: INCB13739 Still Leads by 1.05 kcal/mol — Inside the Noise: A Vina Benchmark of 11β-HSD1 Inhibitors on 4C7K and the Wrong-Target Run That Had to Be Discarded
abstract: Type 2 diabetes affected about 537 million adults worldwide in 2021, including about 33 million in Pakistan, and intracellular glucocorticoid excess is one of the metabolic drivers that existing therapies do not directly target. The enzyme 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 (11beta-HSD1) converts inactive cortisone into active cortisol inside liver and adipose tissue, amplifying intracellular glucocorticoid action; its activity is elevated in the adipose tissue of obese rodents and humans and is linked to metabolic syndrome and type 2 diabetes. INCB13739, a selective 11beta-HSD1 inhibitor, showed a positive phase 2 result — 200 mg daily for 12 weeks lowered A1C by 0.6 percent, fasting glucose by 24 mg per decilitre and HOMA-IR by 24 percent versus placebo in 302 patients inadequately controlled on metformin — yet it was never approved, and no 11beta-HSD1 inhibitor has reached approval. We asked whether a standardised automated docking pipeline could rank known sub-nanomolar 11beta-HSD1 inhibitors against INCB13739. The LeadForge pipeline was run live on 6 November 2026; its first target query resolved to the wrong enzyme entirely (AKR1C3, not 11beta-HSD1) and was discarded, and its first structures failed receptor preparation or centred on a detergent molecule. On the corrected target (UniProt P28845, ChEMBL CHEMBL4235, 58 bioactivities) and the corrected centre — the centroid of the co-crystallised inhibitor DZL in PDB 4C7K (1.91 angstrom) — five ligands were docked with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7. INCB13739 scored minus 11.32 kcal per mol; the best lead, CHEMBL3664636 (IC50 0.31 nM), scored minus 10.27 kcal per mol, with the remaining leads at minus 9.69, minus 9.36 and minus 8.55 kcal per mol. INCB13739 still leads on docking by 1.05 kcal per mol, inside Vina's plus-minus 1 to 2 kcal per mol noise, and all four leads are sub-nanomolar by measured IC50, so docking cannot separate them from the reference and the ranking is not a discovery. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head 11beta-HSD1 enzyme inhibition assay of CHEMBL3664636 versus INCB13739 under identical conditions, with a pre-registered rule that a docking margin under 2 kcal per mol predicts no measurable potency advantage; a measured potency difference larger than two-fold would refute that prediction.
summary: Type 2 diabetes affected about 537 million adults worldwide in 2021, including about 33 million in Pakistan, and intracellular glucocorticoid excess is one of the metabolic drivers that existing therapies do not directly target.

title: No Lead Beats Roxadustat Beyond Noise: A Vina Benchmark of PHD2/EGLN1 Inhibitors on 6QGV and the Missing Metal Ion
abstract: Anaemia of chronic kidney disease is treated with erythropoiesis-stimulating agents that require injection and iron supplementation, and hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitors (HIF-PHIs) offer an oral alternative that raises endogenous erythropoietin and improves iron mobilisation. Roxadustat, the first HIF-PHI, is approved in China, Japan and the European Union but was refused approval in the United States in 2021 on benefit-risk grounds, and the search for a better PHD2 inhibitor continues. We asked whether a standardised, fully automated docking pipeline could rank known PHD2/EGLN1 inhibitors against roxadustat. The LeadForge pipeline was run live on 6 November 2026; its first target query resolved to the wrong enzyme entirely (P4HTM, not PHD2) and was discarded, and its first structure contained the HIF peptide sitting in the binding pocket, so every ligand scored positive and that run was discarded too. On the corrected target (UniProt Q9GZT9, ChEMBL CHEMBL5697, 57 bioactivities) and the corrected structure — PDB 6QGV (1.40 Å), grid centred exactly on the co-crystallised inhibitor J2H centroid [20.93, -0.43, 33.59] — five ligands were docked with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7. The best-scoring lead, CHEMBL5572635, scored -8.38 kcal/mol against roxadustat's -7.50 kcal/mol, a margin of 0.88 kcal/mol that lies inside Vina's ±1-2 kcal/mol scoring noise. The most potent compound by measured IC50, CHEMBL3115307 (0.65 nM), scored -7.54 kcal/mol, effectively tied with roxadustat. No lead beats roxadustat beyond noise, and every score is metal-free because the pipeline's receptor preparation drops the active-site metal ion that roxadustat-class inhibitors chelate, so Vina cannot score the chelation interaction at all. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head PHD2 enzyme inhibition assay of CHEMBL5572635 against roxadustat under identical conditions, with a pre-registered rule that a docking margin under 2 kcal/mol predicts no measurable potency advantage — a measured potency advantage greater than 2-fold for either compound, or a Fe-chelation-aware rescoring that reverses the ranking, would refute the claim that no lead here beats roxadustat.
summary: Anaemia of chronic kidney disease is treated with erythropoiesis-stimulating agents that require injection and iron supplementation, and hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitors (HIF-PHIs) offer an oral alternative that raises endogenous erythropoietin and improves iron mobilisation.

title: Two Leads "Beat" Macozinone by Docking and Lose by 1.23 kcal/mol of Noise: A Vina Benchmark of DprE1 Inhibitors on 4P8N and the Covalent Binding Vina Cannot See
abstract: Tuberculosis made about 10.8 million people ill in 2023 and killed about 1.25 million, and the search for shorter, safer regimens continues. Macozinone (PBTZ169), a benzothiazinone in phase 2 trials, covalently inhibits the Mycobacterium tuberculosis enzyme DprE1, blocking arabinan synthesis and cell-wall biogenesis, but its covalent binding cannot be modelled by standard docking, so a docking benchmark against it risks measuring the method rather than the molecule. We ran the LeadForge pipeline live on 6 November 2026 (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → Vina docking): target DprE1 (UniProt P9WJF1, strain ATCC 25618 / H37Rv, ChEMBL CHEMBL3804751, 58 bioactivities), structure PDB 4P8N at 1.79 Å, grid centred exactly on the co-crystallised non-covalent inhibitor R57 ([16.51, −20.97, 1.7]), and five ligands docked with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 under an identical protocol. Two known DprE1 actives "beat" macozinone on docking — CHEMBL4763381 at −12.05 kcal/mol and CHEMBL4752208 at −11.74 kcal/mol, against macozinone at −10.82 kcal/mol — margins of 1.23 and 0.92 kcal/mol, inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise. But both leads are far weaker by measured potency: IC50 200 nM and 140 nM against macozinone's 10 nM, so the docking ranking is inverted against experiment, and a third "lead", CHEMBL3330226 at −10.96 kcal/mol, is macozinone itself entered twice, scoring −10.96 versus −10.82 as the query. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head DprE1 enzyme inhibition assay of CHEMBL4763381 against macozinone under identical conditions, with a pre-registered rule that a docking margin under 2 kcal/mol predicts no measurable advantage; a measured potency advantage for the lead, or covalent docking showing macozinone binds Cys387 far more tightly than Vina suggests, would refute the claim that the docking win is only a measurement of Vina's limits.
summary: Tuberculosis made about 10.8 million people ill in 2023 and killed about 1.25 million, and the search for shorter, safer regimens continues.

title: No ALK Inhibitor in This Set Beats Alectinib Beyond Vina Noise: A Benchmark Docking of Known ALK Inhibitors on PDB 4Z55
abstract: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) rearrangements drive about 3–7% of non-small cell lung cancers, and alectinib is the standard first-line inhibitor: in the ALEX phase III trial it gave median progression-free survival of 34.8 months versus 10.9 months for crizotinib. Resistance still emerges, most often through the G1202R solvent-front mutation, and the search for better ALK inhibitors continues. We asked whether a standardised, automated docking pipeline could rank known ALK inhibitors against alectinib on the ALK catalytic domain. The LeadForge pipeline was run live on 6 November 2026 (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → Vina): target UniProt Q9UM73, ChEMBL CHEMBL4247, 50 bioactivities retrieved, 25 compounds passed the similarity screen and 26 were ranked. Five ligands were docked with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on PDB 4Z55 (1.55 Å), grid centred exactly on the co-crystallised ligand 4LO centroid [−21.06, 9.75, −7.5], box 22.5 Å, exhaustiveness 8, three poses, best of three reported. Two leads scored above alectinib: CHEMBL3946496 at −10.16 kcal/mol (IC50 0.32 nM) and CHEMBL3929615 at −10.10 kcal/mol (IC50 0.3 nM), versus alectinib at −9.48 kcal/mol — margins of 0.62–0.68 kcal/mol, inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol scoring noise, so no lead beats alectinib beyond noise. The most potent compound by measured IC50, CHEMBL3892880 (0.168 nM), scored only −9.54 kcal/mol, 0.06 kcal/mol above alectinib — docking cannot separate these compounds. All five ligands were PAINS-clean. The falsifiable next step is a head-to-head ALK kinase inhibition assay of CHEMBL3946496 against alectinib under identical conditions, plus docking and assay on G1202R-mutant ALK: a measured potency advantage greater than 2-fold, or retained activity against G1202R, would confirm a real lead; a tie would refute the docking margin.
summary: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) rearrangements drive about 3–7% of non-small cell lung cancers, and alectinib is the standard first-line inhibitor: in the ALEX phase III trial it gave median progression-free survival of 34.8 months versus 10.9 months for crizotinib.

title: Awake Glymphatic Enhancement: A Vasomechanic Clearance Framework for Alzheimer's Prevention — Synthesis of Two 2026 Human Trials and a Falsifiable Trial Design
abstract: Two human trials published in 2026 closed the two halves of the same question. Dagum et al. showed in a randomised crossover trial (n = 39) that normal sleep, versus sleep deprivation, raises morning plasma amyloid-beta and tau — the first direct human evidence that the glymphatic system clears Alzheimer's proteins from brain to blood during sleep. Three days ago, Tuunanen et al. showed that the same clearance can be switched on while awake: one session of sublingual nitroglycerin (0.5 mg) plus Piezo1-targeted whole-body vibration (22–50 Hz, 37 min) in 29 healthy adults raised serum amyloid-beta 40 by 32.2%, amyloid-beta 42 by 34.6% and glial fibrillary acidic protein by 30.5%, with larger proteins unchanged — a size-selective efflux consistent with a ~68 kDa gate. We recompute the published results: the three low-molecular-weight markers give a mean per-session efflux of +32.4%, the effect sizes are dz = 0.52–0.53, and the blood-pressure drop that drives the effect correlates with the biomarker rise (r = −0.49 to −0.63). Vibration alone produced no significant brain-fluid change and nitric oxide alone recapitulated sleep physiology, so the combination — not either arm alone — is the intervention. We propose the awake-clearance framework: a 12-week, sham-controlled trial of thrice-weekly vasomechanic sessions in amyloid-positive adults aged 55–75, powered (n = 58 per arm, 138 with attrition) from the published effect sizes, with plasma p-tau217 as the primary endpoint. The falsifiable claim: if the per-session efflux is real clearance, plasma p-tau217 must fall versus sham; if it does not fall while per-session amyloid-beta 42 efflux rises, the plasma rises are redistribution, not clearance, and the prevention rationale fails. This paper is a synthesis and a trial design, not a treatment recommendation — no brain amyloid, cognition or durability data exist yet.
summary: Two human trials published in 2026 closed the two halves of the same question.
